title.zh: 卷500 列傳二百八十七 遗逸一
title.raw: 卷500 列傳二百八十七 遗逸一

sentences.zh: 李清李模梁以樟王世德閻爾梅萬壽祺鄭與僑

translations.literal: Li Qing, Li Mo, Liang Yizhang, Wang Shide, Yan Ermei, Wan Shouqi, Zheng Yuqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qing, Li Mo, Liang Yizhang, Wang Shide, Yan Ermei, Wan Shouqi, and Zheng Yuqiao.

sentences.zh: 曹元方莊元辰王玉藻李長祥王正中董守諭

translations.literal: Cao Yuanfang, Zhuang Yuanchen, Wang Yuzao, Li Changxiang, Wang Zhengzhong, Dong Shouyu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yuanfang, Zhuang Yuanchen, Wang Yuzao, Li Changxiang, Wang Zhengzhong, and Dong Shouyu.

sentences.zh: 陸宇弟宇巇江漢方以智子中德等錢澄之

translations.literal: Lu Yu, his younger brother Yu Xi, Jiang Han, Fang Yizhi and his son Zhongde, and others, Qian Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu, his younger brother Yu Xi, Jiang Han, Fang Yizhi and his son Zhongde, Qian Chengshi, and others.

sentences.zh: 惲日初郭金台硃之瑜沈光文陳士京吳祖錫

translations.literal: Yun Richu, Guo Jintai, Zhu Zhiyu, Shen Guangwen, Chen Shijing, Wu Zuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Richu, Guo Jintai, Zhu Zhiyu, Shen Guangwen, Chen Shijing, and Wu Zuxi.

sentences.zh: 太史公伯夷列傳，憂憤悲嘆，百世下猶想見其人。

translations.literal: In the Grand Historian's biography of Bo Yi, grief, indignation, sorrow, and lamentation are such that even a hundred generations later one still longs to behold the man.
translations.idiomatic: In the Grand Historian's biography of Bo Yi, grief and indignation pour forth in such lament that even a hundred generations later readers still yearn to meet the man face to face.

sentences.zh: 伯夷、叔齊扣馬而諫，既不能行其志，不得已乃遁西山，歌采薇，痛心疾首，豈果自甘餓死哉？

translations.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi seized the horse's bridle to remonstrate; unable to carry out their purpose, they had no choice but to flee to Mount Xi, singing "Gathering Ferns," heartsick to the core—could they truly have been content to starve themselves to death?
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi and Shu Qi seized the horse's bridle to remonstrate; when they could not put their purpose into effect, they had no choice but to withdraw to Mount Xi and sing "Gathering Ferns," sick at heart—could they truly have welcomed starvation?

sentences.zh: 清初，代明平賊，順天應人，得天下之正，古未有也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qing, replacing the Ming and pacifying the rebels, conforming to Heaven and responding to the people, they obtained the Mandate in its proper form—such a thing had never existed in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Qing, the dynasty replaced the Ming, pacified the rebels, aligned with Heaven, and won the people's assent, securing the Mandate in its proper form—something without precedent in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 天命既定，遺臣逸士猶不惜九死一生以圖再造，及事​​不成，雖浮海入山，而回天之志終不少衰。

translations.literal: Once the Mandate of Heaven was settled, surviving ministers and reclusive scholars still did not spare themselves from death nine times over for one chance at life in order to plot restoration; when the enterprise failed, though they fled across the sea or into the mountains, their will to turn back Heaven never diminished in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Mandate was settled, loyalist ministers and reclusive scholars still risked death again and again to restore the dynasty; and when the cause failed, though they took to the sea or the mountains, their will to turn the heavens back never slackened.

sentences.zh: 迄於國亡已數十年，呼號奔走，逐墜日以終其身，至老死不變，何其壯歟！

translations.literal: Down to several decades after the state's fall, they cried out and rushed about, pursuing their cause day by day until the end of their lives, unchanging even unto old age and death—how magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Even decades after the fall of the state they still cried out and rushed about, pressing their cause day after day to the end of their lives, unchanging until death—how magnificent!

sentences.zh: 今為遺逸傳，凡明末遺臣如李清等，逸士如李孔昭等，分著於篇，雖寥寥數十人，皆大節凜然，足風後世者也。

translations.literal: Now this is made the Biographies of Recluses; in all, late-Ming surviving ministers such as Li Qing, and reclusive scholars such as Li Kongzhao, are set forth in separate entries; though only a few dozen in number, all bear lofty integrity and suffice to inspire later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Here we compose the Biographies of Recluses: late-Ming loyalist ministers such as Li Qing and reclusive scholars such as Li Kongzhao are treated in separate entries; though only a few dozen in all, each displays lofty integrity enough to inspire posterity.

sentences.zh: 至黃宗羲等已見儒林傳，魏禧等已見文苑傳，餘或分見於孝友及藝術諸傳，則當比而觀之，以見其全焉。

translations.literal: As for Huang Zongxi and others, they already appear in the Biographies of Confucian Scholars; Wei Xi and others already appear in the Biographies of Literary Men; the rest appear in part in the biographies of filial sons and friends and of artists—these should be read together to see them whole.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongxi and others already appear in the Biographies of Confucian Scholars, Wei Xi and others in the Biographies of Literary Men, and the rest in part among the filial, friendly, and artistic biographies; those accounts should be read together for the full picture.

sentences.zh: 李清，字心水，號映碧，興化人。

translations.literal: Li Qing, style name Xinshui, sobriquet Yingbi, was a native of Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qing, styled Xinshui and known as Yingbi, was from Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 天啟辛酉舉人，崇禎辛未進士，授寧波府推官。

translations.literal: In the xinyou year of the Tianqi reign he passed the provincial examination; in the xinwei year of the Chongzhen reign he became a jinshi and was appointed investigating censor of Ningbo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the xinyou year of Tianqi and became a jinshi in the xinwei year of Chongzhen, after which he was appointed investigating censor of Ningbo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 考最，擢刑科給事中，同日上兩疏：一言禦外敵當戰守兼治，不當輕言款；

translations.literal: Rated highest in evaluation, he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments; on the same day he submitted two memorials: one saying that in repelling foreign enemies one should combine warfare and defense and should not lightly speak of negotiated peace;
translations.idiomatic: Rated highest in his evaluation, he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments and on the same day submitted two memorials: one argued that repelling foreign enemies required both fighting and defending together, and that negotiated peace should not be proposed lightly;

sentences.zh: 禦內寇當剿撫並用，不當專言撫。

translations.literal: in repelling internal bandits one should employ both suppression and pacification and should not speak only of pacification.
translations.idiomatic: the other argued that internal rebels should be met with both suppression and pacification, not pacification alone.

sentences.zh: 一言治獄不宜置失入，而獨罪失出，因論尚書劉之鳳不職狀。

translations.literal: One said that in administering punishments one should not overlook wrongful convictions while punishing only wrongful releases, and on that basis discussed the misconduct of Minister Liu Zhifeng.
translations.idiomatic: The second held that in criminal justice wrongful convictions should not be ignored while only wrongful releases were punished, and on that basis criticized Minister Liu Zhifeng for dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 尋以天旱，复疏言此用刑鍛鍊刻深所致，語侵尚書甄淑，淑遂劾清把持，詔鐫級，調浙江布政司照磨。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of drought, he again memorialized that this came of excessively harsh and forged punishments, his words impugning Minister Zhen Shu; Shu then impeached Qing for domineering conduct, and an edict reduced his rank and transferred him to the post of registrar in the Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, citing the drought, he memorialized again that the disaster stemmed from excessively harsh and coerced punishments, implicating Minister Zhen Shu; Shu then impeached Qing for domineering conduct, and an edict reduced his rank and transferred him to registrar in the Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commission.

sentences.zh: 無何，淑敗，即家起吏科給事中。

translations.literal: Before long Shu fell, and Qing was summoned from home to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shu fell from power, and Qing was summoned from home to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 疾朝臣日競門戶，疏言：「國家門戶有二：北門之鎖鑰，以三協為門戶；

translations.literal: Distressed that court officials daily contended in faction, he memorialized: "The state has two gateways: the lock and key of the northern gate are the Three Xie;
translations.idiomatic: Distressed by the daily factional strife among court officials, he memorialized: "The state has two gateways: the northern gate's lock and key lie in the Three Xie;

sentences.zh: 陪京之扃鍵，以兩淮為門戶。

translations.literal: the bolt and bar of the secondary capital are the Two Huai.
translations.idiomatic: the secondary capital's bolt and bar lie in the Two Huai.

sentences.zh: 置此不問，而閧堂斫穴，長此安底？」

translations.literal: Leave these unheeded while brawling in the hall and hacking at one another's dens—how can this go on?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet these are left unattended while men brawl in the hall and hack at one another's dens—how can this end well?"

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but no reply came.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，福王建號南京，遷工科都給事中。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, the Prince of Fu established his reign-title at Nanjing, and Qing was transferred to chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, the Prince of Fu proclaimed his reign at Nanjing, and Qing was promoted to chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Works.

sentences.zh: 見朝政日壞，官方大亂，乃疏言：「大仇未雪，凡乘國難以拜官者，義將慚慟入地，宜急更前轍，以圖光復。」

translations.literal: Seeing court affairs daily worsen and officialdom in great disorder, he memorialized: "The great vengeance is not yet avenged; all who have taken office by exploiting the national calamity ought in righteousness to die of shame and grief; Your Majesty should urgently change course to plan restoration."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing court affairs worsen daily and officialdom fall into chaos, he memorialized: "The great vengeance remains unavenged; all who have taken office by exploiting the national calamity ought in righteousness to die of shame; Your Majesty should urgently change course and plan restoration."

sentences.zh: 又憤時議以偏安自足，抗疏曰：「昔宋高之南渡也，說者謂其病於意足，若陛下於今日，其何足之有？

translations.literal: Again, indignant that current opinion took partial security as sufficient, he submitted a forceful memorial: "When Emperor Gaozong of Song crossed south, critics said his malady lay in being content in intent; if Your Majesty today, what is there to be content about?
translations.idiomatic: Indignant that contemporaries took partial security as sufficient, he submitted a forceful memorial: "When Emperor Gaozong of Song crossed south, critics said his malady was contentment; what, for Your Majesty today, is there to be content about?

sentences.zh: 以河、洛為豐、沛，則恭皇之舊封也，為恭皇所已有而不有，則不足；

translations.literal: Take the He and Luo as Feng and Pei—that was the former fief of the Respectful Emperor; what the Respectful Emperor already possessed and yet does not possess is insufficiency;
translations.idiomatic: Take the He and Luo as Feng and Pei—that was the Respectful Emperor's former fief; what he already possessed and yet lacks is insufficiency;

sentences.zh: 以金陵為長安，則高帝之始基也，為高帝所全有而不有，則不足。

translations.literal: take Jinling as Chang'an—that was the High Emperor's founding base; what the High Emperor wholly possessed and yet does not possess is insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: take Jinling as Chang'an—that was the High Emperor's founding base; what he wholly possessed and yet lacks is insufficiency.

sentences.zh: 臣深望陛下無忘痛恥，以此志為中外倡也。

translations.literal: Your servant deeply hopes Your Majesty will not forget bitter shame and will take this resolve as a model for court and realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant deeply hopes Your Majesty will not forget bitter shame and will make this resolve a model for court and realm alike.

sentences.zh: 儻陛下弛於上，則諸臣必逸於下，先帝之深仇，將安得而復哉？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty slackens above, then the ministers will surely grow lax below—how will the late emperor's deep vengeance ever be avenged?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty slackens above, the ministers will grow lax below—how then will the late emperor's deep vengeance ever be avenged?

sentences.zh: 且宋之南渡，猶走李成，擒楊麼，以靖內製外。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the Song southward crossing they still routed Li Cheng and captured Yang Mo, pacifying the interior to control the exterior.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after the Song crossed south they still routed Li Cheng and captured Yang Mo, pacifying the interior to control the exterior.

sentences.zh: 今則獻、瑤交熾，兩川危於累卵，汀、潮、南贛，並以警聞。

translations.literal: Now Zhang Xianzhong and Li Dingguo blaze together; the two Shu are as precarious as piled eggs; Ting, Chao, and southern Gan all send alarms.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhang Xianzhong and Li Dingguo rage together; the two Shu hang by a thread; Ting, Chao, and southern Gan all report alarms.

sentences.zh: 北有既毀之室，南無可怡之堂，臣竊為陛下危之！」

translations.literal: In the north there is a house already ruined; in the south there is no hall in which to take comfort—your servant privately fears for Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: In the north the house is already ruined; in the south there is no hall where one may take comfort—your servant privately trembles for Your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 疏上，報聞而已。

translations.literal: The memorial went up; acknowledgment of receipt was all.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but only acknowledgment of receipt followed.

sentences.zh: 有司始諡莊烈帝為思宗，清言廟號同於漢後主禪，請易之。

translations.literal: The authorities first gave the posthumous title Sizong to the Zhuanglie Emperor; Qing said the temple name was the same as that of the Later Lord of Han, Liu Shan, and requested that it be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities first gave the posthumous title Sizong to the Zhuanglie Emperor; Qing argued that the temple name duplicated that of Liu Shan, the Later Lord of Han, and asked that it be changed.

sentences.zh: 又請補諡太子、二王及開國、靖難並累朝死諫諸臣，或以為迂，歎曰：「士大夫廉恥喪盡矣！

translations.literal: He also requested supplementary posthumous titles for the crown prince, the two princes, and the founding, Jingnan, and successive generations of officials who died remonstrating—some thought this pedantic, and he sighed: "The integrity and shame of scholar-officials are utterly lost!
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for supplementary posthumous titles for the crown prince, the two princes, and officials of the founding, Jingnan, and later reigns who died remonstrating; some called this pedantic, and he sighed: "Scholar-officials have lost all sense of integrity and shame!

sentences.zh: 不於此時顯微闡幽，激發忠義之氣，更復何望耶？」

translations.literal: If at this time one does not bring the obscure to light and rouse the spirit of loyalty and righteousness, what further hope is there?"
translations.idiomatic: If we do not bring the obscure to light now and rouse the spirit of loyalty and righteousness, what hope remains?"

sentences.zh: 清事兩朝，凡三居諫職，章奏後先數十上，並寢閣不行。

translations.literal: Qing served two dynasties and thrice held remonstrating office; memorials submitted in succession numbered several tens, all shelved and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Qing served two dynasties and held remonstrating office three times; several dozen memorials in succession were all shelved without effect.

sentences.zh: 尋遷大理寺左寺丞，遣祀南鎮，行甫及杭，而南都失守矣。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to left assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and dispatched to sacrifice at the Southern Sacred Peak; he had just reached Hangzhou when the Southern Capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made left assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and sent to sacrifice at the Southern Sacred Peak; he had just reached Hangzhou when the Southern Capital fell.

sentences.zh: 乃由間道趨隱松江，又渡江寓高郵，久乃歸故園，杜門不與人事。

translations.literal: He then took bypaths to hide in Songjiang, crossed the river and lodged in Gaoyou, and after a long time returned to his old garden, closing his door and having no dealings with the world.
translations.idiomatic: He then took secret routes to hide in Songjiang, crossed the river and lodged in Gaoyou, and after a long interval returned to his old home, closing his door to the world.

sentences.zh: 當道屢薦不起，凡​​三十有八年而歿。

translations.literal: Local authorities repeatedly recommended him, but he would not rise; in all, thirty-eight years passed before he died.
translations.idiomatic: Local authorities repeatedly recommended him, but he would not serve; thirty-eight years later he died.

sentences.zh: 清忠義蓋出天性，莊烈帝之變，適在揚州，聞之，號慟幾絕。

translations.literal: Qing's loyalty and righteousness sprang from his inborn nature; the Zhuanglie Emperor's calamity happened to occur while he was in Yangzhou—on hearing of it he wailed until nearly dead.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's loyalty and righteousness sprang from inborn nature; the Zhuanglie Emperor's calamity occurred while he was in Yangzhou, and on hearing of it he wailed until he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 自是每遇三月十九日，必設位以哭。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever the nineteenth day of the third month came, he invariably set out a seat and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, on the nineteenth day of the third month each year, he invariably set out a seat and wept.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾家世受國恩，吾以外吏，蒙先帝簡擢，涓埃未報。」

translations.literal: He once said: "My family for generations received the state's grace; I, a minor official, was singled out and promoted by the late emperor, yet not the slightest debt has been repaid."
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "My family for generations received the state's grace; I, a minor official, was singled out and promoted by the late emperor, yet I have repaid not the slightest debt."

sentences.zh: 國亡後，守其硜硜，有死無二，蓋以此也。

translations.literal: After the state's fall he kept to his unyielding course, faithful unto death without a second thought—this was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the state he held to his unyielding course, faithful unto death without a second thought—and this was why.

sentences.zh: 晚著書自娛，尤潛心史學，為史論若干卷，又刪注南、北二史，編次南渡錄等書，藏於家。

translations.literal: In his later years he wrote books for his own pleasure and especially devoted himself to historical studies, composing several fascicles of historical essays, also abridging and annotating the two histories of the Southern and Northern Dynasties and compiling works such as the Record of the Southern Crossing, all kept at home.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he wrote for his own pleasure and devoted himself especially to historical studies, producing several fascicles of historical essays, abridging and annotating the two histories of the Southern and Northern Dynasties, and compiling works such as the Record of the Southern Crossing, all kept in his household.

sentences.zh: 李模，字子木，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Li Mo, style name Zimu, was a native of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mo, styled Zimu, was from Wu County.

sentences.zh: 天啟乙丑進士，授東莞知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the yichou year of Tianqi, he was appointed magistrate of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the yichou year of Tianqi, he was appointed magistrate of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 考最，入為御史。

translations.literal: Rated highest in evaluation, he entered the capital as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Rated highest in his evaluation, he entered the capital as a censor.

sentences.zh: 因劾論中官，謫南京國子監典籍。

translations.literal: Because he impeached and discussed eunuch officials, he was demoted to archivist of the Nanjing Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Because he impeached eunuch officials, he was demoted to archivist of the Nanjing Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 福王立，封四鎮為侯、伯，模上言：「擁立時，陛下不以得位為利，諸臣何敢以定策為功？

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned and the four garrisons were enfeoffed as marquises and earls, Mo memorialized: "At the time of supporting Your Majesty's enthronement, Your Majesty did not regard gaining the throne as a benefit—how dare the ministers claim merit for settling the succession?
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned and the four garrisons were enfeoffed as marquises and earls, Mo memorialized: "When Your Majesty was enthroned, you did not regard gaining the throne as a benefit—how dare ministers claim merit for settling the succession?

sentences.zh: 甚至侯、伯之封，輕加鎮將。

translations.literal: Even marquisates and earldoms were lightly bestowed on garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Even marquisates and earldoms were lightly bestowed on garrison commanders.

sentences.zh: 夫諸將事先帝未收桑榆之效，事陛下未彰汗馬之績，方應戴罪，何有勳勞？

translations.literal: The generals in serving the late emperor had not achieved the effect of the evening mulberry; in serving Your Majesty they had not shown the merit of horses sweating in battle—they ought rather to bear guilt; what merit had they?
translations.idiomatic: The generals had not served the late emperor to the last, nor shown conspicuous merit under Your Majesty—they ought rather to bear guilt; what merit had they?

sentences.zh: 使諸將果忠義者，必先慰先帝殉國之靈，而後可膺陛下延世之賞。」

translations.literal: If the generals were truly loyal and righteous, they must first console the spirit of the late emperor who died for the state, and only then could they receive Your Majesty's reward for prolonging the dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: If they were truly loyal and righteous, they must first console the spirit of the late emperor who died for the state, and only then receive Your Majesty's reward for prolonging the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: Acknowledgment of receipt was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 尋改為河南道御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to censor of the Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to censor of the Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 馬、阮亂政，歎曰：「事無可為矣！」

translations.literal: When Ma Shiying and Ruan Dayue threw the government into disorder, he sighed: "The affair can no longer be done!"
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Shiying and Ruan Dayue threw the government into disorder, he sighed: "Nothing more can be done!"

sentences.zh: 即請告，不復出。

translations.literal: He immediately requested leave and never came forth again.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately requested leave and never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 杜門里居，三十年如一日。

translations.literal: He closed his door and lived at home for thirty years as one day.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his door and lived at home for thirty years without change.

sentences.zh: 幼與徐汧為總角交，汧死國事，為卹其家而存其孤，不渝舊好。

translations.literal: In youth he and Xu Kan were playmates; Kan died for the state, and Mo mourned his family and preserved his orphan, not betraying their old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and Xu Kan had been close friends since childhood; when Kan died for the state, Mo mourned his family and preserved his orphan, never betraying their old bond.

sentences.zh: 年八十，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the age of eighty he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty he died at home.

sentences.zh: 梁以樟，字公狄，清苑人。

translations.literal: Liang Yizhang, style name Gongdi, was a native of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yizhang, styled Gongdi, was from Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 與兄以棻、弟以桂，並知名，時號「三梁」。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Yifen and younger brother Yigui he was alike renowned, and the age called them "the Three Liangs."
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Yifen and younger brother Yigui were all renowned, and their contemporaries called them "the Three Liangs."

sentences.zh: 以樟負異才，八歲讀書家塾中，值壁裂，作壁裂歌云：「壁猛裂，龍驚出。」

translations.literal: Yizhang possessed extraordinary talent; at eight, reading in the family school, when a wall cracked he composed a "Song of the Cracked Wall," saying: "The wall fiercely splits—the dragon startles forth."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhang possessed extraordinary talent; at eight, while reading in the family school, he saw a wall crack and composed a "Song of the Cracked Wall": "The wall splits apart—the startled dragon emerges."

sentences.zh: 見者大奇之。

translations.literal: Those who saw it greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: All who saw it marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 十六歲補弟子員，受知左光斗。

translations.literal: At sixteen he became a student member and won the recognition of Zuo Guangdou.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he became a licentiate and won the recognition of Zuo Guangdou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎己卯舉鄉試第一，明年成進士。

translations.literal: In the jimao year of Chongzhen he placed first in the provincial examination; the next year he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the jimao year of Chongzhen he placed first in the provincial examination, and the next year became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 命試騎射，進士皆書生，夙不習，以樟獨躍馬彎弓，矢三發，的皆應弦破，觀者嘆異。

translations.literal: Ordered to test horsemanship and archery, the jinshi were all scholars unaccustomed to it from of old; Yizhang alone leaped on a horse, bent the bow, and with three arrows loosed broke the target each time the string sounded—onlookers sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to test horsemanship and archery, the jinshi were all scholars unaccustomed to such skills; Yizhang alone leaped on a horse, bent the bow, and with three arrows broke the target each time—onlookers marveled.

sentences.zh: 即授河南太康知縣。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed magistrate of Taikang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed magistrate of Taikang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 中原盜起十餘年，所在荼毒，督撫莫能辦，率倡撫議，苟且幸無事，盜且服且叛。

translations.literal: Bandits had risen in the Central Plain for more than ten years; everywhere they ravaged; governors-general and governors could not cope and generally advocated pacification, taking temporary relief in the hope of no trouble, while bandits submitted and rebelled by turns.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits had ravaged the Central Plain for more than ten years; governors-general and governors could not cope and generally advocated pacification, taking temporary relief while bandits submitted and rebelled by turns.

sentences.zh: 而河南比年大旱蝗，人相食，民益蜂起為盜。

translations.literal: Henan in recent years had suffered great drought and locusts; men ate one another, and the people swarmed ever more into banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Henan in recent years had suffered drought and locusts; men ate one another, and ever more people swarmed into banditry.

sentences.zh: 人為以樟危，僉都御史史可法以其有經世略，獨勸之行。

translations.literal: People considered Yizhang in peril; the censor-in-chief Shi Kefa, because he had statecraft in view, alone urged him to go.
translations.idiomatic: People thought Yizhang was in peril; Censor-in-Chief Shi Kefa alone urged him to go, judging that he had a talent for statecraft.

sentences.zh: 抵任，探知境內賊凡三十六窟，於是練鄉勇，修城堡，嚴保甲；

translations.literal: On reaching his post he investigated and learned that within the district there were thirty-six bandit lairs in all; he then trained local militia, repaired fortresses, and tightened the baojia system;
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he learned that the district held thirty-six bandit lairs; he then trained local militia, repaired fortresses, and tightened the baojia system;

sentences.zh: 募死士，入賊巢。

translations.literal: recruited men willing to die, and sent them into bandit nests.
translations.idiomatic: recruited men willing to die and sent them into bandit nests.

sentences.zh: 伺賊出入。

translations.literal: They watched the bandits' comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: They watched the bandits' movements.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜半馳風雪中，帥健兒密搗賊壘，賊驚佚，擒其渠，毀巢而歸。

translations.literal: Once at midnight he galloped through wind and snow, leading stalwart men in a secret strike on a bandit camp; the bandits fled in alarm, he captured their chief, destroyed the nest, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Once at midnight he galloped through wind and snow, leading stalwart men in a secret raid on a bandit camp; the bandits fled in alarm, he captured their chief, destroyed the nest, and returned.

sentences.zh: 居半載，境內賊悉平。

translations.literal: Within half a year bandits throughout the district were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year bandits throughout the district were pacified.

sentences.zh: 調商丘，時李自成犯開封，不能破，乃東攻歸德。

translations.literal: Transferred to Shangqiu, at that time Li Zicheng attacked Kaifeng and could not take it, so he turned east to attack Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shangqiu, he found Li Zicheng attacking Kaifeng; unable to take it, Li turned east to attack Guide.

sentences.zh: 以樟嬰城血戰三日夜，城陷，妻張率家人三十口自焚死，事具明史。

translations.literal: Yizhang defended the city in bloody battle for three days and nights; the city fell, and his wife Zhang led thirty members of the household to burn themselves to death—the affair is fully recorded in the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhang defended the city in bloody battle for three days and nights; when it fell, his wife Zhang led thirty members of the household to burn themselves to death—the affair is fully recorded in the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 以樟被重創，僕亂屍中，死复甦，商民救之出，奔淮上，被逮讞請室。

translations.literal: Yizhang suffered grave wounds and lay among the corpses in the rout; dead, he revived; merchants rescued him and he fled to the Huai region, where he was arrested and sent to the prison for capital cases.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhang suffered grave wounds and lay among the corpses in the rout; though seemingly dead he revived; merchants rescued him and he fled to the Huai region, where he was arrested and sent to the capital prison.

sentences.zh: 賊入潼關，复渡河東犯，京師震動。

translations.literal: The bandits entered Tong Pass and again crossed the river to attack east; the capital was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels entered Tong Pass and again crossed the river to attack eastward; the capital was shaken.

sentences.zh: 以樟乃從獄中上疏：「請皇太子撫軍南京，輔以重臣，假便宜從事，係人心。

translations.literal: Yizhang then from prison submitted a memorial: "I request that the crown prince take command of the army at Nanjing, assisted by great ministers and granted discretionary authority, to bind the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: From prison Yizhang submitted a memorial: "I request that the crown prince take command of the army at Nanjing, assisted by great ministers and granted discretionary authority, to bind the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 倡召豪傑義旅，大起勤王兵。

translations.literal: Propose summoning heroic volunteers and raise in force armies to rescue the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Propose summoning heroic volunteers and raise armies in force to rescue the throne.

sentences.zh: 擇宗室賢才，分建要地，而重督撫權，行方鎮遺意，合力拒。」

translations.literal: Select talented members of the imperial clan, establish them at key points, and restore weight to the powers of governors-general and governors, following the intent of the Tang and Song frontier commissioners, to resist together."
translations.idiomatic: Select talented members of the imperial clan, establish them at key points, restore weight to the powers of governors-general and governors in the manner of Tang and Song frontier commissioners, and resist together."

sentences.zh: 疏上，執政尼之。

translations.literal: The memorial went up; the chief ministers blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but the chief ministers blocked it.

sentences.zh: 迨出獄，而都城陷。

translations.literal: When he came out of prison, the capital had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he left prison, the capital had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 福王立，以樟自德州、臨清南下，與各郡邑建義文武吏及諸豪士歃血盟，人皆感憤流涕，受約束待命。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, Yizhang came south from Dezhou and Linqing and with civil and military officials of various prefectures and counties who had raised righteous armies and with various eminent men swore a blood oath; all were moved to indignant tears and accepted discipline, awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, Yizhang came south from Dezhou and Linqing and with civil and military officials of various prefectures and counties who had raised righteous armies, together with eminent local men, swore a blood oath; all wept in indignant grief and accepted discipline, awaiting orders.

sentences.zh: 渡淮見可法，因建議：「山東、河北為江南籓蔽，若無山東、河北，是無中原、江北，無中原、江北，區區江南，豈能自守耶？

translations.literal: Crossing the Huai he saw Kefa and therefore proposed: "Shandong and Hebei are the screen of Jiangnan; without Shandong and Hebei there is no Central Plain or north of the river; without the Central Plain and north of the river, how can the narrow Jiangnan defend itself?
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Huai he saw Shi Kefa and proposed: "Shandong and Hebei are Jiangnan's screen; without them there is no Central Plain or country north of the river; without the Central Plain and the north, how can narrow Jiangnan defend itself?

sentences.zh: 今宜於河南北、山東，設三大鎮，仿唐節度使、宋經制招討使之制，以大臣文武兼資者為之。

translations.literal: Now one should establish three great garrisons north of the Yellow River in Henan and in Shandong, following the Tang system of military commissioners and the Song system of pacification commissioners, with great ministers of combined civil and military talent to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Now three great garrisons should be established north of the Yellow River in Henan and in Shandong, following the Tang military commissioners and the Song pacification commissioners, with great ministers of combined civil and military talent to command them.

sentences.zh: 寬其文法，使自為戰守，而閣部大治兵，居中馭之。」

translations.literal: Relax legal constraints on them so they may fight and defend for themselves, while the Grand Secretariat and ministries greatly organize troops and control them from the center."
translations.idiomatic: Relax legal constraints so they may fight and defend on their own, while the Grand Secretariat and ministries organize troops and control them from the center."

sentences.zh: 又言：「北方人心向順，宜及時撫為我用，否則忠者不能支，黠者反戈相向矣。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The hearts of the north incline toward submission; one should promptly win them for our use, otherwise the loyal cannot hold out and the cunning will turn their blades against us."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Northern hearts incline toward submission; they should be won promptly for our use, otherwise the loyal cannot hold out and the cunning will turn their blades against us."

sentences.zh: 前後奏記百數十。

translations.literal: Memorials before and after numbered more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials before and after numbered more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 而馬士英專政，貨鬻官爵，用逆黨阮大鋮為兵部尚書，競立門戶，斥忠讜之士，君臣日夜酣樂。

translations.literal: But Ma Shiying monopolized government, sold offices and ranks for profit, employed the traitor-faction member Ruan Dacheng as Minister of War, vied to form factions, and expelled loyal and forthright men; ruler and ministers nightly reveled.
translations.idiomatic: But Ma Shiying monopolized government, sold offices and ranks, appointed the traitor-faction member Ruan Dacheng Minister of War, vied in faction, expelled loyal and forthright men, and ruler and ministers nightly reveled.

sentences.zh: 左良玉、高傑、劉澤清等各擁兵跋扈，莫能製。

translations.literal: Zuo Liangyu, Gao Jie, Liu Zeqing, and others each held troops and were overbearing; none could control them.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu, Gao Jie, Liu Zeqing, and others each held troops arrogantly, and none could control them.

sentences.zh: 以樟知事不可為，憤鬱成疾，辭去。

translations.literal: Yizhang knew the affair could not be done, grew ill from indignant grief, and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhang knew nothing more could be done, fell ill from indignant grief, and resigned.

sentences.zh: 可法仍舉以樟為兵部職方司主事，經理開、歸。

translations.literal: Kefa still recommended Yizhang as director in the Bureau of Military Appointments of the Ministry of War, to administer Kaifeng and Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa still recommended Yizhang as director in the Bureau of Military Appointments of the Ministry of War to administer Kaifeng and Guide.

sentences.zh: 未幾，揚州破，可法死，南都相繼潰。

translations.literal: Before long Yangzhou fell, Kefa died, and the Southern Capital collapsed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yangzhou fell, Shi Kefa died, and the Southern Capital collapsed in turn.

sentences.zh: 以樟遂與以棻遯跡寶應之葭湖，買田數十畝，躬耕自給。

translations.literal: Yizhang then with Yifen hid their traces at Jiahu in Baoying, bought several tens of acres of fields, and personally tilled to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhang then withdrew with Yifen to Jiahu in Baoying, bought several tens of acres of land, and personally farmed to support themselves.

sentences.zh: 清初，召用勝國諸臣，以樟年才三十七，朝貴致書勸駕，不應。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qing, when officials of the former dynasty were summoned to serve, Yizhang was only thirty-seven; eminent court figures sent letters urging him to take office, but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qing, when former Ming officials were summoned to serve, Yizhang was only thirty-seven; eminent court figures sent letters urging him to take office, but he did not respond.

sentences.zh: 自築忍冬軒，日與張★M9、孫爾靜講學其中，四方之士，若閻爾梅、王猷定、劉純學、崔干城、僧松隱暨其鄉人王世德父子，時時過以樟劇飲，慷慨激昂，繼以涕泣。

translations.literal: He built his own Honeysuckle Pavilion and daily lectured there with Zhang Jue and Sun Erjing; scholars from the four directions, such as Yan Ermei, Wang Youding, Liu Chunxue, Cui Gancheng, the monk Songyin, and his fellow townsman Wang Shide and his father and son, often visited Yizhang for heavy drinking, passionate and stirring, followed by weeping.
translations.idiomatic: He built his own Honeysuckle Pavilion and daily lectured there with Zhang Jue and Sun Erjing; scholars from all directions—Yan Ermei, Wang Youding, Liu Chunxue, Cui Gancheng, the monk Songyin, and his fellow townsman Wang Shide and his sons—often visited Yizhang for heavy drinking, speaking with passionate fervor followed by tears.

sentences.zh: 晚年偕喬出塵、陳鈺、硃克生、劉中柱結文字社。

translations.literal: In his later years he joined Qiao Chuchen, Chen Yu, Zhu Kesheng, and Liu Zhongzhu to form a literary society.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he joined Qiao Chuchen, Chen Yu, Zhu Kesheng, and Liu Zhongzhu to form a literary society.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年七月十五日，端坐作論學數百言，擲筆而卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month of the fourth year of Kangxi, he sat upright, wrote several hundred words on the study of principle, threw down his brush and died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month of the fourth year of Kangxi, he sat upright, wrote several hundred words on the study of principle, threw down his brush, and died at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 世德之子潔、源，集其理學、經濟諸書及詩、古文合為一編，曰梁鷦林先生全書，今傳世者，惟卬否詩集而已。

translations.literal: Shide's sons Jie and Yuan gathered his books on Neo-Confucian learning, statecraft, poetry, and ancient prose into one compilation, titled Complete Works of Mr. Liang Jiaolin; what survives in the world today is only the Yin Fou Poetry Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Shide's sons Jie and Yuan gathered his works on Neo-Confucian learning, statecraft, poetry, and ancient prose into one compilation titled Complete Works of Mr. Liang Jiaolin; only the Yin Fou Poetry Collection survives today.

sentences.zh: 世德，字克承，自號霜皋，北平人。

translations.literal: Shide, style name Kezheng, sobriquet Shuanggao, was a native of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Shide, styled Kezheng and known as Shuanggao, was from Beiping.

sentences.zh: 少襲錦衣衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In youth he inherited the post of vice commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he inherited the post of vice commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 北部陷，拔刀將引決，為僕所奪，妻魏已率婦女赴井死，遂易僧服，與以樟偕隱。

translations.literal: When the north fell, he drew his sword intending to kill himself, but a servant seized it; his wife Wei had already led the women to drown themselves in a well; he then changed into monk's robes and went into hiding with Yizhang.
translations.idiomatic: When the north fell, he drew his sword to kill himself, but a servant wrested it away; his wife Wei had already led the women to their deaths in a well; he then donned monk's robes and went into hiding with Yizhang.

sentences.zh: 嘗憤野史誣罔，不可傳信後世，欷歔扼腕，作崇禎遺錄一卷，自序之，康熙間修明史，有司錄其副本上史館。

translations.literal: Once indignant that unofficial histories spread falsehoods and could not be trusted by posterity, he sighed and wrung his hands, wrote one fascicle of Chongzhen's Last Record with his own preface; when the Ming History was compiled during Kangxi, officials submitted a copy to the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Indignant that unofficial histories spread falsehoods unfit to be trusted by posterity, he sighed and wrung his hands, wrote one fascicle of Chongzhen's Last Record with his own preface, and during the Kangxi compilation of the Ming History officials submitted a copy to the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，卒，年八十有一。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi he died, aged eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 子源，以手藁殉葬。

translations.literal: His son Yuan had the manuscript buried with him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan had the manuscript buried with him.

sentences.zh: 閻爾梅，字用卿，號古古，沛縣人。

translations.literal: Yan Ermei, style name Yongqing, sobriquet Gugu, was a native of Pei County.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ermei, styled Yongqing and known as Gugu, was from Pei County.

sentences.zh: 崇禎庚午舉人。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the gengwu year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the gengwu year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷北京，爾梅上書請兵北伐，並儘散家財，結死士，為前驅。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng seized Beijing, Ermei submitted a memorial requesting troops for a northern expedition, and also distributed all his family wealth, gathering men willing to die, to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng seized Beijing, Ermei submitted a memorial requesting troops for a northern expedition, distributed all his family wealth, and gathered men willing to die to serve as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 自成黨武愫至沛，屢使招爾梅，以碎牒大罵下獄，愫敗，乃免。

translations.literal: A Li Zicheng follower, Wu Su, arrived at Pei and repeatedly sent envoys to recruit Ermei; Ermei tore the dispatch to pieces and cursed him, and was thrown into prison; when Su was defeated, he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng's agent Wu Su arrived at Pei and repeatedly sent envoys to recruit Ermei; Ermei tore the dispatch to shreds and cursed him, and was thrown into prison; when Su was defeated, he was released.

sentences.zh: 赴史可法之聘，參軍事，首勸渡河复山東，不聽。

translations.literal: He accepted Shi Kefa's invitation, joined military affairs, and first urged crossing the river to recover Shandong; [Shi Kefa] would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted Shi Kefa's invitation, joined military affairs, and first urged crossing the river to recover Shandong; Shi Kefa would not listen.

sentences.zh: 時高傑為許定國所殺，河南大亂，爾梅又說可法西行鎮撫之。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Jie was killed by Xu Dingguo and Henan was in great disorder; Ermei again urged Kefa to go west to pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Jie was killed by Xu Dingguo and Henan fell into great disorder; Ermei again urged Shi Kefa to go west and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 傑部將約束待命，可法為設提督統其眾，而自退保揚州。

translations.literal: Jie's subordinate generals agreed to await orders; Kefa appointed a grand coordinator to command them and himself withdrew to defend Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's subordinate generals agreed to await orders; Shi Kefa appointed a grand coordinator to command them and himself withdrew to defend Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 爾梅力阻之，請開幕府徐州，號召河南北義勇，得以一成一旅規畫中原。

translations.literal: Ermei strenuously opposed this, requesting to open a headquarters at Xuzhou to summon loyal volunteers from north and south of the [Yellow] River, so that with even one formation and one brigade he could plan for the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Ermei strenuously opposed this, requesting to open a headquarters at Xuzhou to summon loyal volunteers from north and south of the River, so that with even a single regiment he could plan for the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 又請空名告身數百紙，乘時布發，視忠義為鼓勵，俾逋寇叛帥不得以逾時渙散，少有睥睨。

translations.literal: He also requested several hundred blank appointment commissions, to be issued at the opportune moment, viewing loyalty and righteousness as encouragement, so that fleeing bandits and rebel commanders could not exploit the delay to scatter and cast sidelong glances.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested several hundred blank commissions to distribute at the right moment, treating loyalty and righteousness as encouragement so that fleeing bandits and rebel commanders could not exploit the delay to scatter and grow restive.

sentences.zh: 策皆不行，遂貽以書而去。

translations.literal: None of these plans was adopted, so he sent Kefa a letter and departed.
translations.idiomatic: None of these plans was adopted, so he sent Shi Kefa a letter and departed.

sentences.zh: 及可法殉節，爾梅走淮安，就劉澤清、田仰，畫戰守策，復不聽。

translations.literal: When Kefa died for the cause, Ermei fled to Huai'an and sought out Liu Zeqing and Tian Yang, outlining strategies for war and defense; again they would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Kefa died for the cause, Ermei fled to Huai'an and sought out Liu Zeqing and Tian Yang, outlining strategies for war and defense; again they would not listen.

sentences.zh: 師入淮，爾梅率河北壯士伏城外，眾懼阻，羽士陶萬明特庇之。

translations.literal: When the army entered Huai, Ermei led northern-hebei stalwarts to lie in ambush outside the walls; the troops feared obstruction; the Taoist Tao Wanming especially sheltered him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing army entered Huai, Ermei led stalwarts from north of the River to lie in ambush outside the walls; the troops feared obstruction, but the Taoist Tao Wanming especially sheltered him.

sentences.zh: 巡撫趙福星以書招，爾梅痛哭謝之。

translations.literal: Surveillance commissioner Zhao Fuxing recruited him by letter; Ermei wept and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance commissioner Zhao Fuxing recruited him by letter; Ermei wept and declined.

sentences.zh: 乃散其眾，遁海上，祝髮，稱蹈東和尚。

translations.literal: He then dismissed his followers, fled to the sea, tonsured his head, and styled himself Daodong Monk.
translations.idiomatic: He then dismissed his followers, fled to the sea, tonsured his head, and styled himself Daodong Monk.

sentences.zh: 复走山東，聯絡四方魁傑，謀再舉。

translations.literal: He again went to Shandong, contacted champions from all quarters, and plotted another uprising.
translations.idiomatic: He again went to Shandong, contacted champions from all quarters, and plotted another uprising.

sentences.zh: 又至河南，至京師，以山東事發被捕，下濟南獄，脫走還沛。

translations.literal: He also went to Henan and the capital; because the Shandong affair was discovered he was arrested and imprisoned in Jinan; he escaped and returned to Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He also went to Henan and the capital; when the Shandong affair was discovered he was arrested and imprisoned in Jinan, escaped, and returned to Pei.

sentences.zh: 名捕急，弟爾羹、侄禦九皆就逮，妻、妾同自縊。

translations.literal: Wanted posters were urgent; his younger brother Ergen and nephew Yujiu were both seized; his wife and concubine hanged themselves together.
translations.idiomatic: The hunt for him grew urgent; his younger brother Ergen and nephew Yujiu were both seized; his wife and concubine hanged themselves together.

sentences.zh: 爾梅乃託死夜遁，變名翁深，字藏若，歷遊楚、蜀、秦、晉九省。

translations.literal: Ermei then feigned death and fled by night, changed his name to Weng Shen, styled Cangruo, and traveled through nine provinces: Chu, Shu, Qin, and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Ermei then feigned death and fled by night, changed his name to Weng Shen, styled Cangruo, and traveled through nine provinces—Chu, Shu, Qin, and Jin among them.

sentences.zh: 過關中，與王弘撰等往還。

translations.literal: Passing through Guanzhong, he associated with Wang Hongzuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Guanzhong, he associated with Wang Hongzuan and others.

sentences.zh: 北至榆林，從寧夏入蘭州。

translations.literal: He went north to Yulin, entered Lanzhou from Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He went north to Yulin and entered Lanzhou from Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 凡十年，獄解，始還。

translations.literal: After ten years the prison case was resolved, and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years the prison case was resolved, and he returned home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為仇家所攀，復出亡，龔鼎孳救之，得免。

translations.literal: Before long, an enemy family implicated him and he fled again; Gong Dingzi saved him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an enemy family implicated him and he fled again; Gong Dingzi saved him and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 北謁思陵，又東出榆關。

translations.literal: He went north to pay respects at Sizong's mausoleum, then went east through the Yulin Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He went north to pay respects at Sizong's mausoleum, then went east through the Yulin Pass.

sentences.zh: 還京，會顧炎武，复遊塞外。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he met Gu Yanwu and again traveled beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital, he met Gu Yanwu and again traveled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 至太原，訪傅山，結歲寒之盟。

translations.literal: Reaching Taiyuan, he visited Fu Shan and formed the cold-year covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Taiyuan, he visited Fu Shan and pledged friendship in adversity.

sentences.zh: 爾梅久奔走，歷艱險，不少阻。

translations.literal: Ermei had long rushed about, enduring hardships and dangers, without much discouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Ermei had long rushed about, enduring hardships and dangers, with little discouragement.

sentences.zh: 後見大勢已去，知不可為，乃還沛。

translations.literal: Later seeing the great trend was already gone and knowing nothing could be done, he returned to Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeing the great trend was already gone and knowing nothing more could be done, he returned to Pei.

sentences.zh: 寄於酒，醉則罵座。

translations.literal: He took refuge in wine; when drunk he cursed those present.
translations.idiomatic: He took refuge in wine; when drunk he cursed those present.

sentences.zh: 常慨然曰：「吾先世未有仕者，國亡，破家為報仇，天下震動。

translations.literal: He often said with emotion: "My ancestors never held office; when the state fell I ruined my family to avenge it, and the realm was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: He often said with emotion: "My ancestors never held office; when the state fell I ruined my family to avenge it, and the realm was shaken.

sentences.zh: 事雖終不成，疾風勁草，布衣之雄足矣！」

translations.literal: Though the enterprise ultimately failed, in a fierce wind the tough grass [stands firm]—a hero in plain cloth suffices!"
translations.idiomatic: Though the enterprise ultimately failed, in a fierce wind the tough grass stands firm—a hero in plain cloth suffices!"

sentences.zh: 遂高歌起舞。

translations.literal: Then he sang loudly and danced.
translations.idiomatic: Then he sang loudly and danced.

sentences.zh: 泣數行下。

translations.literal: Tears streamed down several lines.
translations.idiomatic: Tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 居數歲卒。

translations.literal: After several years residing there, he died.
translations.idiomatic: After several years there, he died.

sentences.zh: 年七十有七。

translations.literal: Aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 爾梅博學善詩，有白耷山人集。

translations.literal: Ermei was broadly learned and skilled at poetry; he has the Baiga Shanren Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Ermei was broadly learned and skilled at poetry; he left the Baiga Shanren Collection.

sentences.zh: 萬壽祺，字介若，世稱年少先生，徐州人。

translations.literal: Wan Shouqi, style name Jieruo, known in the world as Master Shaonian, was a native of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Shouqi, styled Jieruo and known in the world as Master Shaonian, was from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 與爾梅同郡，又同歲生，同舉鄉試，志節皆

translations.literal: He was from the same commandery as Ermei, born in the same year, passed the provincial examination together; their integrity of purpose was all
translations.idiomatic: He was from the same commandery as Ermei, born in the same year, and passed the provincial examination together; their integrity of purpose was the same,

sentences.zh: 同，既同舉事。

translations.literal: the same, and they also jointly raised the standard together.
translations.idiomatic: and they also jointly raised the standard in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 南都破，江以南義師云起。

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital fell, loyal armies rose like clouds south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Capital fell, loyal armies rose like clouds south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 沈自炳、戴之俊、錢邦芑起陳湖，黃家瑞、陳子龍起泖，吳易起笠澤，皆與會師，謀恢復。

translations.literal: Shen Zibing, Dai Zhijun, and Qian Bangqian rose at Chenhu; Huang Jiarui and Chen Zilong rose at Mao; Wu Yi rose at Lize—all joined forces and planned restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zibing, Dai Zhijun, and Qian Bangqian rose at Chenhu; Huang Jiarui and Chen Zilong rose at Mao; Wu Yi rose at Lize—all joined forces and planned restoration.

sentences.zh: 兵潰，壽祺被執，不屈，將及難，有陰救之者，囚系月餘，得脫。

translations.literal: When the army was routed, Shouqi was captured, refused to submit; about to face disaster, someone secretly rescued him; imprisoned for over a month, he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was routed, Shouqi was captured and refused to submit; about to face execution, someone secretly rescued him; after more than a month in prison, he escaped.

sentences.zh: 乃渡江歸隱，築室浦西，妻徐、子睿，灌園以自給。

translations.literal: He then crossed the river and returned to seclusion, built a dwelling west of the ford, with wife Xu and son Rui, tending gardens to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed the river and returned to seclusion, built a dwelling west of the ford, and with his wife Xu and son Rui tended gardens to support themselves.

sentences.zh: 髡首被僧衣，自稱明志道人、沙門慧壽，而飲酒食肉如故。

translations.literal: He shaved his head and wore monk's robes, styling himself Monk Mingzhi and Shramana Huishou, yet drank wine and ate meat as before.
translations.idiomatic: He shaved his head and wore monk's robes, styling himself Monk Mingzhi and Shramana Huishou, yet drank wine and ate meat as before.

sentences.zh: 時渡江而南，訪知舊，吊故壘。

translations.literal: He would cross the river south to visit old friends and mourn former camps.
translations.idiomatic: He would cross the river south to visit old friends and mourn former camps.

sentences.zh: 遺民故老過淮陰者，亦輒造草堂，流連歌哭，或淹留旬月。

translations.literal: Surviving subjects and old elders passing through Huaiyin would also visit his thatched hall, lingering in song and weeping, sometimes staying a month or more.
translations.idiomatic: Surviving subjects and old elders passing through Huaiyin would also visit his thatched hall, lingering in song and weeping, sometimes staying a month or more.

sentences.zh: 雖隱居，固未嘗一日忘世也。

translations.literal: Though in reclusion, he never for a single day forgot the world.
translations.idiomatic: Though in reclusion, he never for a single day forgot the world.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Shunzhi he died.

sentences.zh: 壽祺善詩、文、書、畫，旁及琴、劍、棋、曲、雕刻、刺繡，亦靡弗工妙。

translations.literal: Shouqi was skilled at poetry, prose, calligraphy, and painting, and also excelled at zither, sword, chess, opera, carving, and embroidery—nothing failed to reach exquisite mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqi was skilled at poetry, prose, calligraphy, and painting, and also excelled at the zither, sword, chess, opera, carving, and embroidery—nothing failed to reach exquisite mastery.

sentences.zh: 爾梅論有明一代書，推為第一。

translations.literal: Ermei, in discussing Ming calligraphy, ranked him first.
translations.idiomatic: Ermei, in discussing Ming calligraphy, ranked him first.

sentences.zh: 著有隰西草堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Xixi Thatched Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Xixi Thatched Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 初，爾梅、壽祺同謀舉事，一起江北，一起江南，先後相呼應。

translations.literal: Initially Ermei and Shouqi plotted an uprising together—one rose north of the River, one south of the River, calling to each other in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Ermei and Shouqi plotted an uprising together—one rose north of the River, one south of the River, calling to each other in turn.

sentences.zh: 及事敗，爾梅出走，思得一當。

translations.literal: When the enterprise failed, Ermei fled, seeking one success.
translations.idiomatic: When the enterprise failed, Ermei fled, seeking one chance at success.

sentences.zh: 壽祺留江、淮觀世變，不幸先死。

translations.literal: Shouqi remained on the Yangtze and Huai to observe the changes of the times; unfortunately he died first.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqi remained on the Yangtze and Huai to observe the changes of the times; unfortunately he died first.

sentences.zh: 爾梅獨奔走三十餘年，亦終無所就。

translations.literal: Ermei alone rushed about for more than thirty years, yet ultimately achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Ermei alone rushed about for more than thirty years, yet ultimately achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 後世稱「徐州二遺民」，常為之太息雲。

translations.literal: Later generations call them "the Two Surviving Subjects of Xuzhou" and often sigh deeply for them.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations call them "the Two Recluses of Xuzhou" and often sigh deeply for them.

sentences.zh: 鄭與僑，字惠人，號確菴，濟寧人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuqiao, style name Huiren, sobriquet Que'an, was a native of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqiao, styled Huiren and known as Que'an, was from Jining.

sentences.zh: 五歲父歿，母張以祖遺田讓之仲，獨取遺書一篋授僑，曰：「兒讀此，可飽也！」

translations.literal: At five his father died; his mother Zhang gave the ancestral fields to the second uncle, keeping only one basket of inherited books, which she gave Yuqiao, saying: "My child, read these and you can be fed!"
translations.idiomatic: At five his father died; his mother Zhang gave the ancestral fields to the second uncle, keeping only one basket of inherited books, which she gave Yuqiao, saying: "My child, read these and you will never go hungry!"

sentences.zh: 與僑發奮力學，崇禎丙子舉於鄉。

translations.literal: Yuqiao applied himself with determination to study and passed the provincial examination in the bingzi year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqiao applied himself with determination to study and passed the provincial examination in the bingzi year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 時流寇充斥山左，與僑以濟寧為漕艘咽喉地，倡義與城守張世臣、舉人孟瑄並力殺賊，城賴以完。

translations.literal: At that time roaming bandits filled Shandong; Yuqiao, because Jining was the throat of the grain transport fleet, initiated righteous action and together with Zhang Shichen, who defended the city, and provincial graduate Meng Xuan fought the bandits with united strength; the city was preserved intact because of this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time roaming bandits filled Shandong; because Jining was the throat of the grain transport fleet, Yuqiao initiated righteous action and, together with city defender Zhang Shichen and provincial graduate Meng Xuan, fought the bandits with united strength; the city was preserved intact.

sentences.zh: 有賊郭升者，將至濟寧州，吏議迎款，囑與僑草表，力拒乃止。

translations.literal: A bandit named Guo Sheng was about to arrive at Jining Prefecture; officials debated welcoming him with submission and commissioned Yuqiao to draft the memorial; he forcefully refused and they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A bandit named Guo Sheng was about to arrive at Jining Prefecture; officials debated welcoming him with submission and commissioned Yuqiao to draft the memorial; he forcefully refused and they stopped.

sentences.zh: 及賊至，與僑率鄉人殲之，遂徙家淮陽。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, Yuqiao led the township people to annihilate them, then moved his household to Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits arrived, Yuqiao led the township people to annihilate them, then moved his household to Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 史可法方開府淮上，聞與僑名，奏為儀真令，而吏部以其前守濟寧功，改除揚州府推官。

translations.literal: Shi Kefa had just opened his headquarters on the Huai; hearing Yuqiao's name, he memorialized for him to be magistrate of Yizhen; but the Board of Personnel, because of his earlier merit defending Jining, changed the appointment to judicial assistant of Yangzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa had just opened his headquarters on the Huai; hearing Yuqiao's name, he memorialized for him to be magistrate of Yizhen; but the Board of Personnel, because of his earlier merit defending Jining, changed the appointment to judicial assistant of Yangzhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 揚州為興平伯高傑列籓地，其將卒多驕橫，稍不當意，抽刀剚人，與僑悉裁之以法。

translations.literal: Yangzhou was the fief territory of Xingping Earl Gao Jie; his officers and soldiers were mostly arrogant and overbearing; at the slightest displeasure they would draw knives and stab people; Yuqiao restrained them all by law.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou was the fief territory of Xingping Earl Gao Jie; his officers and soldiers were mostly arrogant and overbearing; at the slightest displeasure they would draw knives and stab people; Yuqiao restrained them all by law.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史何綸薦以推官監江、海軍，駐通州。

translations.literal: Surveillance censor He Lun recommended him as judicial assistant supervising the river and sea armies, stationed at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance censor He Lun recommended him as judicial assistant supervising the river and sea armies, stationed at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 江南失守，與僑奉母之武林，總督張存仁、經略洪承疇奇其才，欲官之，皆謝不起。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan fell, Yuqiao took his mother to Wulin; Governor-General Zhang Cunren and frontier commissioner Hong Chengchou admired his talent and wished to appoint him; he declined all offers.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan fell, Yuqiao took his mother to Wulin; Governor-General Zhang Cunren and frontier commissioner Hong Chengchou admired his talent and wished to appoint him; he declined all offers.

sentences.zh: 後歸濟上，立社教授生徒，絕口不談時事。

translations.literal: Later he returned to the Ji region, established a literary society to teach students, and never spoke of current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to the Ji region, established a literary society to teach students, and never spoke of current affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘗遍遊秦、晉、川、蜀、荊、楚、吳、越諸勝，著有確菴稿、丹照集、爭光集、濟寧遺事、秦邊記要等書。

translations.literal: He once toured widely through the scenic places of Qin, Jin, Chuan, Shu, Jing, Chu, Wu, and Yue, and authored Que'an Drafts, Danzhao Collection, Zhengguang Collection, Jining Reminiscences, Record of the Qin Frontier, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: He once toured widely through the scenic places of Qin, Jin, Chuan, Shu, Jing, Chu, Wu, and Yue, and authored Que'an Drafts, Danzhao Collection, Zhengguang Collection, Jining Reminiscences, Record of the Qin Frontier, and other books.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十有四。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 自為壙志。

translations.literal: He wrote his own tomb inscription.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his own tomb inscription.

sentences.zh: 曹元方，字介皇，海鹽人。

translations.literal: Cao Yuanfang, style name Jiehuang, was a native of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yuanfang, styled Jiehuang, was from Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 父履泰，明兵部侍郎，以忠直著。

translations.literal: His father Lütai was an assistant minister of War in the Ming, renowned for loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lütai was an assistant minister of War in the Ming, renowned for loyalty and uprightness.

sentences.zh: 元方，崇禎癸未進士，南京建號，授常熟知縣。

translations.literal: Yuanfang became a jinshi in the guiwei year of Chongzhen; when Nanjing established its reign-title he was appointed magistrate of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang became a jinshi in the guiwei year of Chongzhen; when Nanjing established its reign he was appointed magistrate of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 時大學士馬士英擅國政，有薦元方署職方司事者，士英亦藉元方名，冀往謁附己，元方訖不往。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Secretary Ma Shiying monopolized state affairs; someone recommended Yuanfang as acting director in the Bureau of Military Appointments; Shiying also hoped to use Yuanfang's reputation, expecting him to come pay court and attach himself; Yuanfang never went.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Secretary Ma Shiying monopolized state affairs; someone recommended Yuanfang as acting director in the Bureau of Military Appointments; Shiying also hoped to use Yuanfang's reputation, expecting him to come pay court and attach himself; Yuanfang never went.

sentences.zh: 上疏言原遵定制補外吏，語侵士英，士英怒，卒與令常熟。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying he wished to follow established practice and take an exterior post; his words impugned Shiying; Shiying was angered but ultimately let him take office at Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying he wished to follow established practice and take an exterior post; his words impugned Shiying; Shiying was angered but ultimately let him take office at Changshu.

sentences.zh: 常熟為吳中煩劇邑最，當金陵草創，所在兵與民交狃無寧晷。

translations.literal: Changshu was among the most troublesome and demanding counties of Wu; when Jinling was first founded, everywhere soldiers and civilians were mutually habituated to violence without a moment's peace.
translations.idiomatic: Changshu was among the most troublesome and demanding counties of Wu; when Jinling was first founded, everywhere soldiers and civilians were mutually habituated to violence without a moment's peace.

sentences.zh: 元方措兵餉，惜民力，俱帖然，邑稱治。

translations.literal: Yuanfang arranged military supplies and husbanded the people's strength; all became settled; the county was said to be well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang arranged military supplies and husbanded the people's strength; all became settled, and the county was said to be well governed.

sentences.zh: 金陵敗，棄官歸，履泰先獲譴謫戍，亦適歸。

translations.literal: When Jinling was defeated he abandoned office and returned; Lütai had earlier been condemned and exiled to frontier garrison, and also happened to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinling fell he abandoned office and returned; Lütai had earlier been condemned and exiled to frontier garrison, and also happened to return.

sentences.zh: 父子相謂，於義不可晏然以居。

translations.literal: Father and son said to each other that by principle they could not live at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son said to each other that by principle they could not live at ease.

sentences.zh: 元方先變姓名，間道入閩，至建寧，謁唐王。

translations.literal: Yuanfang first changed his name and surname, took a secret route into Fujian, reached Jianning, and had audience with the Prince of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang first changed his name and surname, took a secret route into Fujian, reached Jianning, and had audience with the Prince of Tang.

sentences.zh: 即授吏部文選司主事，晉驗封司郎中。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed director in the Bureau of Civil Appointments of the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to chief in the Bureau of Seals.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed director in the Bureau of Civil Appointments of the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to chief in the Bureau of Seals.

sentences.zh: 頃之，履泰亦由海道至，即授太常卿，晉兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon Lütai also arrived by sea route, immediately appointed minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, promoted to vice minister of the Right in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lütai also arrived by sea, was immediately appointed minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and promoted to vice minister of the Right in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 父子俱以忠義激發，間關來，一時咸偉之。

translations.literal: Father and son both were inspired by loyalty and righteousness, coming through hardships together; for a time all admired them.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son both were inspired by loyalty and righteousness, coming through hardships together; for a time all admired them.

sentences.zh: 當是時，鄭芝龍久以桀寇內附，崇其秩號，姑息為養驕，至是益甚，志叵測。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Zhilong had long since submitted from within as a fierce bandit; the court exalted his rank and title and indulgently fed his arrogance; by now this was even worse and his intentions were unfathomable.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zheng Zhilong had long since submitted from within as a fierce bandit; the court exalted his rank and title and indulgently fed his arrogance; by now this was even worse and his intentions were unfathomable.

sentences.zh: 元方抗疏，自請出視江上師，閱封守，欲從外為重內計。

translations.literal: Yuanfang submitted a forceful memorial, requesting himself to go out and inspect the armies on the river, review border defense, intending to strengthen the interior from without.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang submitted a forceful memorial, requesting himself to go out and inspect the armies on the river and review border defense, intending to strengthen the interior from without.

sentences.zh: 得召對，加御史銜，賜白金，揮涕以行。

translations.literal: He was summoned for audience, granted the title of censor, given silver, and set out weeping.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned for audience, granted the title of censor, given silver, and set out weeping.

sentences.zh: 至浦城，則江上潰兵接踵狼狽下，元方倉卒走，計後圖。

translations.literal: Reaching Pucheng, routed soldiers from the river came down one after another in disarray; Yuanfang fled in haste, planning for later.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Pucheng, routed soldiers from the river came down one after another in disarray; Yuanfang fled in haste, planning for later.

sentences.zh: 履泰從唐王趨贛州，遇兵，投身崖石下，絕复甦。

translations.literal: Lütai followed the Prince of Tang toward Ganzhou; encountering soldiers, he threw himself beneath cliff rocks and lost consciousness, then revived.
translations.idiomatic: Lütai followed the Prince of Tang toward Ganzhou; encountering soldiers, he threw himself beneath cliff rocks, lost consciousness, and then revived.

sentences.zh: 舁至僧舍，展轉至浦城，父子得相見。

translations.literal: Carried to a monk's quarters, he went by stages to Pucheng, and father and son were able to meet.
translations.idiomatic: Carried to a monk's quarters, he went by stages to Pucheng, and father and son were able to meet.

sentences.zh: 履泰疾甚，先歸，旋卒於家。

translations.literal: Lütai was gravely ill, returned home first, and soon died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Lütai was gravely ill, returned home first, and soon died at home.

sentences.zh: 元方聞，乃亟歸，微服挈母及妻子行，寄食旅舍中。

translations.literal: Hearing this Yuanfang hurried home, in plain dress taking his mother, wife and children, lodging at inns for food.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Yuanfang hurried home, in plain dress taking his mother, wife, and children, lodging at inns for food.

sentences.zh: 久之，事稍定，卜居硤石村，築草堂，自號耘庵。

translations.literal: After a long time affairs slightly settled; he chose residence at Xiashi Village, built a thatched hall, and styled himself Yun'an.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time affairs slightly settled; he chose residence at Xiashi Village, built a thatched hall, and styled himself Yun'an.

sentences.zh: 以老卒，年八十有二。

translations.literal: He died of old age, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died of old age at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 莊元辰，字起貞，晚字頑菴，鄞人，學者稱漢曉先生。

translations.literal: Zhuang Yuanchen, style name Qizhen, in his later years style name Wanan, was a native of Yin; scholars called him Master Hanxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Yuanchen, styled Qizhen and in later years Wanan, was from Yin; scholars called him Master Hanxiao.

sentences.zh: 賦性嚴凝，不隨人唯阿。

translations.literal: By nature stern and austere, he did not follow others in flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and austere by nature, he would not truckle to others.

sentences.zh: 崇禎丁丑進士，授南京太常博士。

translations.literal: In the dingchou year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi and was appointed erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingchou year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi and was appointed erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 甲申之變，一日七至中樞史可法之門，促以勤王，福王立，議推科臣，總憲劉宗周、掌科章正宸皆舉元辰為首，而馬士英密遣私人致意曰：「博士曷不持門下刺上謁相公？

translations.literal: At the crisis of Jiashen he visited Grand Secretary Shi Kefa's gate seven times in one day, urging him to march to the emperor's aid; when the Prince of Fu was enthroned, merit was discussed among censorate officials—Censor-in-Chief Liu Zongzhou and chief supervising secretary Zhang Zhengchen both ranked Yuanchen first—but Ma Shiying secretly sent a private agent with this message: "Doctor, why not take a visiting card from your patron and pay a call on the Grand Secretary?
translations.idiomatic: At the crisis of Jiashen he visited Grand Secretary Shi Kefa's gate seven times in one day, urging him to march to the emperor's aid; when the Prince of Fu was enthroned and censorate posts were discussed, Censor-in-Chief Liu Zongzhou and chief supervising secretary Zhang Zhengchen both ranked Yuanchen first—but Ma Shiying secretly sent a private agent with this message: "Doctor, why not take a visiting card from your patron and pay a call on the Grand Secretary?

sentences.zh: 掌科必無他屬。」

translations.literal: The chief supervising secretary will surely have no other choice."
translations.idiomatic: The chief supervising secretary will surely have no other choice."

sentences.zh: 峻拒之。

translations.literal: He sternly refused.
translations.idiomatic: He sternly refused.

sentences.zh: 中旨僅授刑部主事。

translations.literal: An edict from the center appointed him only a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: An edict from the center appointed him only a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 已而阮大鋮欲興同文之獄，元辰曰：「禍將烈矣！」

translations.literal: Before long Ruan Dacheng wished to revive the Tongwen case; Yuanchen said: "Disaster is about to blaze forth!"
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ruan Dacheng wished to revive the Tongwen case; Yuanchen said: "Disaster is about to blaze forth!"

sentences.zh: 遽行，未幾而留都亡。

translations.literal: He departed at once; before long the Southern Capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: He departed at once; before long the Southern Capital fell.

sentences.zh: 錢肅樂之起事也，元辰破家輸餉，時降臣謝三賓為王之仁所脅，以餉自贖。

translations.literal: When Qian Sule raised the standard of revolt, Yuanchen ruined his family to supply funds; at the time the surrendered minister Xie Sanbin, coerced by Wang Zhiren, tried to buy his way out with supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Sule raised the standard of revolt, Yuanchen ruined his family to supply funds; at the time the surrendered minister Xie Sanbin, coerced by Wang Zhiren, tried to buy his way out with supplies.

sentences.zh: 及肅樂與之仁赴江上，三賓潛招兵，眾疑之。

translations.literal: When Sule and Zhiren went to the river front, Sanbin secretly recruited troops, and the men grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When Sule and Zhiren went to the river front, Sanbin secretly recruited troops, and the men grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 明經王家勤謂肅樂曰：「浙東沿海皆可以舟師達鹽官，倘彼乘風而渡，列城且立潰矣，非分兵留守不可。」

translations.literal: Classicist Wang Jiaqin said to Sule: "Along the coast of eastern Zhe, naval forces can reach Yanguan; if they take advantage of the wind to cross, the cities in a row will collapse at once—troops must be divided to hold the rear."
translations.idiomatic: Classicist Wang Jiaqin said to Sule: "Along the Zhejiang coast, naval forces can reach Yanguan; if the enemy crosses with a fair wind, the cities in a row will collapse at once—troops must be divided to hold the rear."

sentences.zh: 肅樂曰：「是無以易吾莊公者。」

translations.literal: Sule said: "There is no one who could replace our Master Zhuang."
translations.idiomatic: Sule said: "There is no one who could replace our Master Zhuang."

sentences.zh: 於是共推元辰任城守事，分兵千人屬之，以四明驛為幕府，家勤及林時躍參其事。

translations.literal: They then jointly recommended Yuanchen to oversee city defense, assigning him a thousand troops; they made Siming Station his headquarters, with Jiaqin and Lin Shiyue assisting in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: They then jointly recommended Yuanchen to oversee city defense, assigning him a thousand troops; they made Siming Station his headquarters, with Jiaqin and Lin Shiyue assisting.

sentences.zh: 元辰日耀兵巡諸堞裡，人呼為「城門軍」，三賓不敢動。

translations.literal: By day Yuanchen displayed his forces and patrolled the ramparts; people called them the "Gate Guard Army," and Sanbin dared not stir.
translations.idiomatic: By day Yuanchen displayed his forces and patrolled the ramparts; people called them the "Gate Guard Army," and Sanbin dared not stir.

sentences.zh: 乃迎魯王於天台，鄞始解嚴。

translations.literal: They then welcomed the Prince of Lu at Tiantai, and Yin at last lifted martial law.
translations.idiomatic: They then welcomed the Prince of Lu at Tiantai, and Yin at last lifted martial law.

sentences.zh: 晉吏科都給事中，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel and transferred to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel and transferred to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「殿下大仇未雪，舉兵以來，將士宣勞於外，編氓殫藏於內，臥薪嘗之不遑，而數月來，頗安逸樂。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Your Highness's great vengeance is not yet avenged; since raising arms, officers and soldiers have proclaimed their merit outside the walls while the registered people have exhausted their stores within—there is no time even to lie on firewood and taste gall, yet in recent months there has been much ease and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Your Highness's great vengeance is not yet avenged; since raising arms, officers and soldiers have proclaimed their merit in the field while the registered people have exhausted their stores at home—there is no time even to lie on firewood and taste gall, yet in recent months there has been much ease and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 釜魚幕燕，撫事增憂，則晏安何可懷也？

translations.literal: Like fish in a cauldron or swallows under a tent—when I consider affairs my worry only grows; how then can ease and comfort be cherished?
translations.idiomatic: Like fish in a cauldron or swallows under a tent—when I consider affairs my worry only grows; how then can ease and comfort be cherished?

sentences.zh: 敵在門庭，朝不及夕，有深宮養優之心，安得有前席借箸之事，則蒙蔽何可滋也？
