translations.literal: The enemy is at the gate; morning does not know the evening; if there is a heart to nurture actors in the inner palace, how can there be the matter of leaning forward over the mat to borrow chopsticks? Then how can obscuration increase?
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is at the gate and morning does not know the evening; if the heart turns to nurturing actors in the inner palace, how can there be counsel like leaning forward over the mat to borrow chopsticks? How then can blindness to danger grow?

sentences.zh: 天下安危，託命將相，今左右之人，頗能內承色笑，則事權何可移也？

translations.literal: The safety and peril of the realm are entrusted to generals and ministers; now those close at hand are quite able to win smiles within—then how can authority be shifted?
translations.idiomatic: The safety and peril of the realm are entrusted to generals and ministers; now those close at hand are quite able to win smiles within—then how can authority be shifted?

sentences.zh: 五等崇封，有如探囊，有為昔時佐命元臣所不能得者，則恩膏何可濫也？

translations.literal: Enfeoffment to the fifth rank is like reaching into a sack; there are those who could not obtain what former ministers who aided the founding could not obtain—then how can favor be lavished without measure?
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffment to the fifth rank is like reaching into a sack; there are men who win what even founding ministers could not obtain—then how can favor be lavished without measure?

sentences.zh: 陛下試念兩都黍離麥秀之悲，則居處必不安；

translations.literal: Your Majesty, try to recall the grief of the two capitals' millet lament—the place of dwelling will surely be unsettled;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, try to recall the grief of the two capitals' millet lament—then the place of dwelling will surely be unsettled;

sentences.zh: 試念孝陵、長陵銅駝荊棘之慘，則對越必不安；

translations.literal: try to recall the horror of Xiaoling and Changling with bronze camels among brambles—the facing of Heaven will surely be unsettled;
translations.idiomatic: try to recall the horror of Xiaoling and Changling with bronze camels among brambles—then the facing of Heaven will surely be unsettled;

sentences.zh: 試念青宮二王之辱，則撫王子何以為情；

translations.literal: try to recall the humiliation of the Eastern Palace and the two princes—then how can one stroke the prince's hair and remain composed;
translations.idiomatic: try to recall the humiliation of the Eastern Palace and the two princes—then how can one stroke the prince's hair and remain composed;

sentences.zh: 試念江乾將士列邦生民之困，則衣食可以俱廢。」

translations.literal: try to recall the distress of officers and soldiers on the river and the people of the myriad states—then food and clothing may both be cast aside."
translations.idiomatic: try to recall the distress of officers and soldiers on the river and the people of the myriad states—then food and clothing may both be cast aside."

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, acknowledgment was returned.

sentences.zh: 已又言中旨用人之非，累有封駁，王不能用。

translations.literal: He later also criticized improper appointments by edict from the center, repeatedly issuing rebuttals; the prince could not employ his advice.
translations.idiomatic: He later also criticized improper appointments by edict from the center, repeatedly issuing rebuttals; the prince could not employ his advice.

sentences.zh: 時三賓夤緣居要，而馬士英又至，元辰言：「士英不斬，國事必不可為！」

translations.literal: At that time Sanbin had wormed his way into important posts, and Ma Shiying had also arrived; Yuanchen said: "Unless Shiying is executed, state affairs can certainly not succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sanbin had wormed his way into important posts, and Ma Shiying had also arrived; Yuanchen said: "Unless Shiying is executed, state affairs can certainly not succeed!"

sentences.zh: 貽書同官黃宗羲、林時對云：「蕞爾氣象，似惟恐其不速盡者，區區憂憤，無事不痛心疾首，以致咳嗽纏綿，形容骨立。

translations.literal: He sent letters to colleagues Huang Zongxi and Lin Shidui, saying: "This petty realm's bearing is as though it only fears not perishing quickly; in small measure I am vexed and indignant, pained at everything to the marrow, so that a cough lingers on and my appearance is bones alone.
translations.idiomatic: He sent letters to colleagues Huang Zongxi and Lin Shidui, saying: "This petty realm's bearing is as though it only fears not perishing quickly; in small measure I am vexed and indignant, pained at everything to the marrow, so that a cough lingers on and my appearance is bones alone.

sentences.zh: 原得以微罪，成其山野。」

translations.literal: I would prefer to be guilty of a minor offense and achieve life in the mountains and wilds."
translations.idiomatic: I would prefer to be guilty of a minor offense and achieve life in the mountains and wilds."

sentences.zh: 遂乞休。

translations.literal: He then requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大兵東下，乃狂走深山中，朝夕野哭。

translations.literal: Before long the great army marched east; he then fled wildly into the deep mountains, weeping in the wilderness morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the great army marched east; he fled wildly into the deep mountains, weeping in the wilderness morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 元辰故美鬚眉，顧盼落落，至是失其面目，巾服似頭陀，一日數徙，莫知所止，山中人亦不復識。

translations.literal: Yuanchen had been handsome with fine brows and beard, his gaze lofty and free; by this time his face was lost, his cap and robe like a dharma-master's; he moved several times in a day, and none knew where he stopped—the mountain people no longer recognized him either.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchen had been handsome with fine brows and beard, his gaze lofty and free; by this time his face was lost, his cap and robe like a dharma-master's; he moved several times in a day, and none knew where he stopped—the mountain people no longer recognized him either.

sentences.zh: 忽有老婦呼其小字曰：「子非念四郎邪？」

translations.literal: Suddenly an old woman called his childhood name: "Are you not Niansilang?"
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly an old woman called his childhood name: "Are you not Niansilang?"

sentences.zh: 因歎曰：「吾晦跡未深，奈何？」

translations.literal: He sighed: "I have not hidden my tracks deeply enough—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed: "I have not hidden my tracks deeply enough—what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 順治四年，疽發背，戒勿藥，曰：「吾死已晚，然及今死猶可。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, an abscess broke out on his back; he warned against medicine, saying: "My death is already late, yet to die even now is still possible."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, an abscess broke out on his back; he warned against medicine, saying: "My death is already late, yet to die even now is still possible."

sentences.zh: 遂卒。

translations.literal: He then died.
translations.idiomatic: He then died.

sentences.zh: 王玉藻，字質夫，江都人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuzao, style name Zhifu, was a native of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuzao, styled Zhifu, was from Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 崇禎癸未進士，授慈溪知縣。

translations.literal: In the guiwei year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiwei year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 少詹項煜以從逆亡命，玉藻及慈民馮元飚均出其門，遂匿於馮氏。

translations.literal: Junior Guardian Xiang Yu fled as a rebel fugitive; Yuzao and Cixi native Feng Yuanbiao had both been his disciples, so he hid at Feng's house.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Guardian Xiang Yu fled as a rebel fugitive; Yuzao and Cixi native Feng Yuanbiao had both been his disciples, so he hid at Feng's house.

sentences.zh: 慈人斃煜於水，玉藻置不問。

translations.literal: The people of Cixi killed Yu in the water; Yuzao took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Cixi killed Yu in the water; Yuzao took no notice.

sentences.zh: 有明士習重闈誼，或以為過，玉藻曰：「吾豈能為向雄之待鍾會哉！

translations.literal: Ming scholars' custom honored examination-year fellowship; some thought it excessive; Yuzao said: "How can I be like Xiang Xiong awaiting Zhong Hui!
translations.idiomatic: Ming scholars' custom honored examination-year fellowship; some thought it excessive; Yuzao said: "How can I be like Xiang Xiong awaiting Zhong Hui!

sentences.zh: 夫君臣之與師友，果孰重？」

translations.literal: Between ruler and minister on the one hand and teacher and friend on the other—which is truly weightier?"
translations.idiomatic: Between ruler and minister on the one hand and teacher and friend on the other—which is truly weightier?"

sentences.zh: 聞者悚然。

translations.literal: Those who heard it were awestruck.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard it were awestruck.

sentences.zh: 金陵破，魯王監國，玉藻乃與沈宸荃起兵，晉御史，仍行縣。

translations.literal: When Jinling fell, the Prince of Lu governed the realm as regent; Yuzao then joined Shen Chenquan in raising troops, was promoted to censor, and still administered the county.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinling fell, the Prince of Lu governed the realm as regent; Yuzao then joined Shen Chenquan in raising troops, was promoted to censor, and still administered the county.

sentences.zh: 复募義勇，請赴江上自劾，略謂：「今恃以自保者，惟錢唐一江，待北兵渡江而後禦，曷若御之於未渡之先？

translations.literal: He again recruited volunteers and requested to go to the river front to impeach himself in a memorial stating roughly: "What we rely on now for self-preservation is only the Qiantang River; to defend after the northern troops have crossed—would it not be better to defend before they have crossed?
translations.idiomatic: He again recruited volunteers and requested to go to the river front, submitting a memorial of self-reproach stating roughly: "What we rely on now for self-preservation is only the Qiantang River; to defend after the northern troops have crossed—would it not be better to defend before they have crossed?

sentences.zh: 臣原以身先之！」

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to take the lead with his own body!"
translations.idiomatic: Your subject wishes to take the lead in person!"

sentences.zh: 乃解縣事，以兵科都給事往軍前。

translations.literal: He then resigned the county post and went to the army front as supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War.
translations.idiomatic: He then resigned the county post and went to the army front as supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War.

sentences.zh: 時駐兵江上者，有方國安、王之仁、孫嘉績、熊汝霖、章正宸、鄭道謙、錢肅樂、沈光文、陳潛夫、黃宗羲，咸各自為軍，兵餉交訌，莫敢先進。

translations.literal: At that time those stationed on the river included Fang Guo'an, Wang Zhiren, Sun Jiaji, Xiong Rulin, Zhang Zhengchen, Zheng Daoqian, Qian Sule, Shen Guangwen, Chen Qianfu, and Huang Zongxi—each commanded his own army; supplies and pay clashed, and none dared advance first.
translations.idiomatic: At that time those stationed on the river included Fang Guo'an, Wang Zhiren, Sun Jiaji, Xiong Rulin, Zhang Zhengchen, Zheng Daoqian, Qian Sule, Shen Guangwen, Chen Qianfu, and Huang Zongxi—each commanded his own army; supplies and pay clashed, and none dared advance first.

sentences.zh: 既不予玉藻以餉，复陳劃地分餉，又不聽，玉藻乃力請還朝。

translations.literal: Since they gave Yuzao no funds, he again memorialized to divide territory for dividing supplies; when they would not listen, Yuzao forcefully requested return to court.
translations.idiomatic: Since they gave Yuzao no funds, he again memorialized to divide territory for dividing supplies; when they would not listen, Yuzao forcefully requested return to court.

sentences.zh: 既入諫垣，上封事十餘，略謂：「北兵之可畏者在勇，而我軍之可慮者在怯，怯由於驕，兵驕由於將驕。

translations.literal: Once he entered the remonstrance office, he submitted more than ten sealed memorials, stating roughly: "What is to be feared in the northern troops is courage; what is to be worried about in our army is cowardice—and cowardice comes from arrogance, and army arrogance from generals' arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered the remonstrance office, he submitted more than ten sealed memorials, stating roughly: "What is to be feared in the northern troops is courage; what is to be worried about in our army is cowardice—and cowardice comes from arrogance, and army arrogance from generals' arrogance.

sentences.zh: 今統兵之將，無汗馬之勞，輒博五等之封，安得不啟以驕心？

translations.literal: The generals in command today, without labor of battle-horses, casually win enfeoffment to the fifth rank—how can this not open the door to arrogant hearts?
translations.idiomatic: The generals in command today, without labor of battle-horses, casually win enfeoffment to the fifth rank—how can this not open the door to arrogant hearts?

sentences.zh: 驕則畏戰，非稍加裁抑，恐無以戢其囂陵之氣。」

translations.literal: Arrogance then fears battle; unless they are slightly restrained and suppressed, I fear there will be no way to curb their overbearing air."
translations.idiomatic: Arrogance then fears battle; unless they are slightly restrained and suppressed, I fear there will be no way to curb their overbearing air."

sentences.zh: 又謂：「宜用海師窺吳淞，以分杭州北兵之勢。

translations.literal: He also stated: "Use naval forces to probe Wusong and divide the pressure of the northern troops at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also stated: "Use naval forces to probe Wusong and divide the pressure of the northern troops at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又劉宗周、祁彪佳諸臣，宜加褒忠之典。」

translations.literal: Again, ministers such as Liu Zongzhou and Qi Bujia should receive posthumous honors for loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Again, ministers such as Liu Zongzhou and Qi Bujia should receive posthumous honors for loyalty."

sentences.zh: 以是不為諸臣所喜，乃力求罷職。

translations.literal: Because of this he was not liked by the various ministers, and he forcefully sought dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he was not liked by the various ministers, and he forcefully sought dismissal.

sentences.zh: 時元辰為太常，固乞留之，謂：「古人折檻旌直，今令直臣去國，豈國家之福！」

translations.literal: At that time Yuanchen was vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and earnestly begged him to remain, saying: "The ancients broke the railing to honor the upright; now to let upright ministers leave the state—is that the state's fortune!"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuanchen was vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and earnestly begged him to remain, saying: "The ancients broke the railing to honor the upright; now to let upright ministers leave the state—is that the state's fortune!"

sentences.zh: 玉藻感其言，供職如初。

translations.literal: Moved by his words, Yuzao resumed duty as before.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his words, Yuzao resumed duty as before.

sentences.zh: 浙東再破，玉藻追魯王蹕，弗及，自投於池，水涸，不得死，乃以黃冠遯於剡溪。

translations.literal: When eastern Zhe fell again, Yuzao pursued the Prince of Lu's traveling court but could not catch up; he threw himself into a pool—the water was dry and he could not die—so he fled in Daoist robes to Shan Stream.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern Zhe fell again, Yuzao pursued the Prince of Lu's traveling court but could not catch up; he threw himself into a pool—the water was dry and he could not die—so he fled in Daoist robes to Shan Stream.

sentences.zh: 資糧俱盡，採野葛為食。

translations.literal: Provisions were entirely exhausted; he gathered wild kudzu for food.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions were entirely exhausted; he gathered wild kudzu for food.

sentences.zh: 妻李，遼東巡撫植女，知書明大義，在浙右時，屢脫簪珥佐軍興；

translations.literal: His wife Li was the daughter of Liaodong governor Li Zhi, literate and understanding great principle; when in western Zhe, she repeatedly sold hairpins and earrings to aid the military effort;
translations.idiomatic: His wife Li was the daughter of Liaodong governor Li Zhi, literate and understanding great principle; when in western Zhe, she repeatedly sold hairpins and earrings to aid the military effort;

sentences.zh: 偕入剡溪，命二子方岐、方嶷拾墮樵，不以窮阨易操。

translations.literal: entering Shan Stream together, she ordered the two sons Fangqi and Fangyi to gather fallen firewood, not changing conduct because of poverty and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: entering Shan Stream together, she ordered the two sons Fangqi and Fangyi to gather fallen firewood, not changing conduct because of poverty and hardship.

sentences.zh: 適四明山寨競起義軍，以書致玉藻，玉藻思乘間入舟山，為偵騎所遏，不果往。

translations.literal: Just then mountain strongholds in Siming rose with righteous armies and sent Yuzao a letter; Yuzao thought to slip in to Zhoushan but was blocked by scout horsemen and could not go.
translations.idiomatic: Just then mountain strongholds in Siming rose with righteous armies and sent Yuzao a letter; Yuzao thought to slip in to Zhoushan but was blocked by scout horsemen and could not go.

sentences.zh: 每臨流讀所作詩，輒激勵慷慨，仰天起舞，或朝夕悲歌，與門人熊亦方相和答。

translations.literal: Whenever he read his own poems by the stream, he was stirred to ardor, dancing toward heaven, or singing grief morning and evening, answering each other with his disciple Xiong Yifang.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he read his own poems by the stream, he was stirred to ardor, dancing toward heaven, or singing grief morning and evening, answering each other with his disciple Xiong Yifang.

sentences.zh: 繼亦方以癲死，玉藻歸隱北湖，誓不易衣去發，作絕詞以逝。

translations.literal: Yifang soon died mad; Yuzao returned to seclusion at North Lake, swore not to change his clothes or cut his hair, and composed a farewell poem before dying.
translations.idiomatic: Yifang soon died mad; Yuzao returned to seclusion at North Lake, swore not to change his clothes or cut his hair, and composed a farewell poem before dying.

sentences.zh: 遺命不冠而斂。

translations.literal: He left orders to be buried without a cap.
translations.idiomatic: He left orders to be buried without a cap.

sentences.zh: 李長祥，字研齋，達州人。

translations.literal: Li Changxiang, style name Yanzhai, was a native of Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changxiang, styled Yanzhai, was from Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎癸未進士。

translations.literal: In the guiwei year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiwei year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 初以諸生練鄉勇助城守，後選庶吉士，吏部薦備將帥之選。

translations.literal: At first as a licentiate he trained local militia to aid in city defense; later he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and the Ministry of Personnel recommended him among candidates for generalship.
translations.idiomatic: At first as a licentiate he trained local militia to aid in city defense; later he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and the Ministry of Personnel recommended him among candidates for generalship.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「天子果用公，計安出？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "If the Son of Heaven truly employs you, Sir, what plan would you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "If the Son of Heaven truly employs you, Sir, what plan would you propose?"

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「不見孫白谷往事乎？

translations.literal: He sighed: "Have you not seen Sun Baigu's past affair?
translations.idiomatic: He sighed: "Have you not seen Sun Baigu's past affair?

sentences.zh: 今惟有請便宜行事，雖有金牌，亦不受進止。

translations.literal: Today there is only to ask leave to act at discretion; even if there were a gold tablet, one would not accept orders to advance or halt.
translations.idiomatic: Today there is only to ask leave to act at discretion; even if there were a gold tablet, one would not accept orders to advance or halt.

sentences.zh: 平賊後，囚首闕下受斧鉞耳！」

translations.literal: After pacifying the bandits, bound and presented at court to receive axe and halberd—that is all!"
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the bandits, bound and presented at court to receive axe and halberd—that is all!"

sentences.zh: 聞者咋舌。

translations.literal: Those who heard it gasped.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard it gasped.

sentences.zh: 賊日逼，上疏請急令大臣輔太子出鎮津門，以提調勤王兵。

translations.literal: As bandits pressed daily, he memorialized urgently requesting that great ministers be ordered immediately to escort the crown prince out to garrison Jin Gate and direct and mobilize troops marching to the emperor's aid.
translations.idiomatic: As bandits pressed daily, he memorialized urgently requesting that great ministers be ordered immediately to escort the crown prince out to garrison Jin Gate and direct and mobilize troops marching to the emperor's aid.

sentences.zh: 不果行，而京師潰，為賊所掠，乘間南奔。

translations.literal: It was not carried out; the capital collapsed and he was plundered by bandits, escaping south in an interval.
translations.idiomatic: It was not carried out; the capital collapsed and he was plundered by bandits, escaping south in an interval.

sentences.zh: 福王立，改監察御史，巡浙鹽。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he was changed to surveillance censor and toured Zhe salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned, he was changed to surveillance censor and toured Zhe salt administration.

sentences.zh: 魯王監國，加右僉都御史，督師西行，而江上師又潰。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu governed as regent, he was added Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and supervised the army marching west, but the river-front army collapsed again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu governed as regent, he was added Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and supervised the army marching west, but the river-front army collapsed again.

sentences.zh: 魯王航海去，長祥以餘眾結寨上虞之東山。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu fled by sea; Changxiang with remnant troops established a stronghold at East Mountain in Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu fled by sea; Changxiang with remnant troops established a stronghold at East Mountain in Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 時浙江諸寨林立，四出募餉，居民苦之。

translations.literal: At that time strongholds in Zhe stood like forests, sallying forth everywhere to levy supplies—the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time strongholds in Zhe stood like forests, sallying forth everywhere to levy supplies—the people suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 獨長祥與張煌言、王翊三營，且屯且耕，井邑不擾。

translations.literal: Only Changxiang, together with Zhang Huangyan and Wang Yi in three camps, both garrisoned and farmed, not disturbing market towns.
translations.idiomatic: Only Changxiang, together with Zhang Huangyan and Wang Yi in three camps, both held garrison farms, not disturbing market towns.

sentences.zh: 監軍鄞人華夏者，為之聯絡佈置，請引舟山之兵，連大蘭諸寨，以定鄞、慈五縣，因下姚江，會師曹娥，合偁山諸寨以下西陵。

translations.literal: Military supervisor Hua Xia of Yin coordinated and arranged for him, requesting to bring Zhoushan troops, link the Dalanshan strongholds, stabilize the five counties of Yin and Cixi, then descend the Yao River, rendezvous at Cao'e, and unite with the Weishan strongholds to move below Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: Military supervisor Hua Xia of Yin coordinated and arranged for him, requesting to bring Zhoushan troops, link the Dalanshan strongholds, stabilize the five counties of Yin and Cixi, then descend the Yao River, rendezvous at Cao'e, and unite with the Weishan strongholds to move below Xiling.

sentences.zh: 僉議奉長祥為盟主，刻期將集，而為降紳謝三賓所發，引兵來攻。

translations.literal: All agreed to make Changxiang league leader and set a date for assembly—but the surrendered gentry Xie Sanbin exposed the plan and led troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed to make Changxiang league leader and set a date for assembly—but the surrendered gentry Xie Sanbin exposed the plan and led troops to attack.

sentences.zh: 前軍張有功被執，死。

translations.literal: Vanguard Zhang Yougong was captured and died.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard Zhang Yougong was captured and died.

sentences.zh: 中軍與百夫長十二人，期以次日縛長祥為獻。

translations.literal: The central army and twelve centurions agreed to bind Changxiang the next day as an offering.
translations.idiomatic: The central army and twelve centurions agreed to bind Changxiang the next day as an offering.

sentences.zh: 晨起，十二人忽自相語：「奈何殺忠臣？」

translations.literal: At morning rise the twelve suddenly said among themselves: "How can we kill a loyal minister?"
translations.idiomatic: At morning rise the twelve suddenly said among themselves: "How can we kill a loyal minister?"

sentences.zh: 折矢扣刃，偕誓而遯。

translations.literal: They broke arrows and sheathed blades, swore together, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They broke arrows and sheathed blades, swore together, and fled.

sentences.zh: 長祥匿丐人舟中，入紹興城。

translations.literal: Changxiang hid in a beggar's boat and entered Shaoxing city.
translations.idiomatic: Changxiang hid in a beggar's boat and entered Shaoxing city.

sentences.zh: 居數日，事益急，复遯至奉化，依平西伯朝先。

translations.literal: After several days, affairs grew still more urgent; he fled again to Fenghua and relied on Earl Pingxi Chaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: After several days, affairs grew still more urgent; he fled again to Fenghua and relied on Earl Pingxi Chaoxian.

sentences.zh: 朝先亦蜀人，得其助，復合眾於夏蓋山，晉兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Chaoxian was also a Shu man; with his help he rallied troops again at Xiagaishan and was promoted Left Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoxian was also a Shu man; with his help he rallied troops again at Xiagaishan and was promoted Left Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 請合朝先之眾，聯絡沿海，以為舟山衛。

translations.literal: He requested to unite Chaoxian's forces and coordinate the coast as a Zhoushan guard.
translations.idiomatic: He requested to unite Chaoxian's forces and coordinate the coast as a Zhoushan guard.

sentences.zh: 張名振忌之，襲殺朝先，長祥僅免。

translations.literal: Zhang Mingzhen resented him, raided and killed Chaoxian; Changxiang barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mingzhen resented him, raided and killed Chaoxian; Changxiang barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 舟山破，亡命江、淮間，總督陳錦捕得之，安置江寧。

translations.literal: When Zhoushan fell, he fled between the Yangtze and Huai; Governor-General Chen Jin captured him and settled him at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhoushan fell, he fled between the Yangtze and Huai; Governor-General Chen Jin captured him and settled him at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 未幾，乘守者之怠，逸去。

translations.literal: Before long, taking advantage of the guards' negligence, he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, taking advantage of the guards' negligence, he escaped.

sentences.zh: 由吳門渡秦郵，奔河北，遍歷宣府、大同，复南下百粵。

translations.literal: He crossed from Suzhou Gate to Qinpost, fled to Hebei, traversed Xuanfu and Datong, then descended again to the Hundred Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed from Suzhou Gate to Qinpost, fled to Hebei, traversed Xuanfu and Datong, then descended again to the Hundred Yue.

sentences.zh: 晚歲，始還居毗陵，築讀易堂以老。

translations.literal: In his later years he at last returned to live at Piling, built the Hall for Reading the Changes, and aged there.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he at last returned to live at Piling, built the Hall for Reading the Changes, and aged there.

sentences.zh: 王正中，字仲撝，保定人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhengzhong, style name Zhongwei, was a native of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhengzhong, styled Zhongwei, was from Baoding.

sentences.zh: 崇禎丁丑進士。

translations.literal: In the dingchou year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingchou year of Chongzhen he became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 魯王監國，以兵部職方司主事攝餘姚縣事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu governed as regent, he served as acting chief clerk in the Bureau of Military Appointments of the Ministry of War while administering Yuyao county affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu governed as regent, he served as acting chief clerk in the Bureau of Military Appointments of the Ministry of War while administering Yuyao county affairs.

sentences.zh: 時義軍猝起，市魁、裡正得一劄付，輒入民舍括金帛，郡縣不敢誰何。

translations.literal: At the time volunteer armies suddenly arose; ward chiefs and village heads, upon receiving a written order, would enter private homes to extort gold and silk, and the prefectures and counties dared not challenge them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time militias were springing up everywhere. Ward chiefs and village heads who received a written requisition would march into people's homes to extort gold and silk, and neither prefectures nor counties dared question them.

sentences.zh: 正中既視事，令各營取餉必經縣，否則以盜論。

translations.literal: Once Zhengzhong had assumed office, he ordered that every camp must obtain provisions through the county; otherwise it would be treated as robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhengzhong took office, he decreed that every camp had to draw rations through the county government—otherwise the act would be prosecuted as theft.

sentences.zh: 總兵陳梧渡海掠餘姚，正中遣民兵擊殺之，諸營大譁，責正中擅殺大將。

translations.literal: Regional commander Chen Wu crossed the sea to plunder Yuyao; Zhengzhong sent militia who attacked and killed him. The camps raised a great outcry, accusing Zhengzhong of killing a general on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Chen Wu crossed the sea to raid Yuyao. Zhengzhong sent militiamen who attacked and killed him. The army camps erupted in protest, denouncing Zhengzhong for having a senior general killed without authorization.

sentences.zh: 黃宗羲言於監國曰：「梧借喪亂以濟其私，致犯眾怒，是賊也。

translations.literal: Huang Zongxi said to the regent: "Wu exploited the turmoil for private gain, provoking universal wrath—he was a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongxi told the regent, "Wu used the chaos to serve his private ends and brought the wrath of all upon himself. He was a bandit.

sentences.zh: 正中守土，當為國保民，何罪之有？」

translations.literal: Zhengzhong guarded his territory and was bound to protect the people for the state—what crime could there be?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzhong held his post and was duty-bound to protect the people for the realm. What crime had he committed?"

sentences.zh: 議乃息。

translations.literal: The debate then subsided.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the uproar died down.

sentences.zh: 張國柱、田仰、荊本徹各率所部過姚江，舳艫蔽空而下，以正中嚴備，不敢犯，皆帖帖趣行。

translations.literal: Zhang Guozhu, Tian Yang, and Jing Benche each led their troops past the Yaojiang River; boats and ships filled the sky as they descended, but because Zhengzhong was rigorously prepared, they did not dare offend and all proceeded submissively on their way.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guozhu, Tian Yang, and Jing Benche each led their forces down the Yaojiang River, their flotilla so dense it darkened the sky. Finding Zhengzhong's defenses ironclad, they dared not provoke him and passed on meekly.

sentences.zh: 國柱後從定海入，縱兵焚掠，正中單騎入其軍，呵止之，國柱迄不得逞。

translations.literal: Later Guozhu entered from Dinghai and let his troops burn and loot; Zhengzhong rode alone into his army, shouted and stopped them, and Guozhu never got his way.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guozhu entered from Dinghai and unleashed his men to burn and plunder. Zhengzhong rode alone into his camp, roared them to a halt, and Guozhu never got what he wanted.

sentences.zh: 尋擢監察御史，諸軍從浙西來會，一聽約束，眾倚之若嚴城焉。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to investigating censor; armies coming from western Zhejiang to assemble all submitted to his discipline, and the multitude relied on him as on a fortified city.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted investigating censor. As armies gathered from western Zhejiang, all submitted to his authority; to the troops he was as dependable as a walled fortress.

sentences.zh: 尋以株連繫獄，論死。

translations.literal: Soon he was implicated by association, imprisoned, and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he was swept up by association, thrown into prison, and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 獄中有閩人柯仲蜅者，精星象，正中欲從受業，援黃霸從夏侯勝授經事為說，數年講習不怠，洞悉天官、律呂、度數諸書，復從黃宗羲學壬遁、孤虛之術。

translations.literal: In prison there was a Fujian man named Ke Zhongfu, skilled in stars and omens; Zhengzhong wished to study under him, citing Huang Ba learning the classics from Xiahou Sheng in prison as precedent. For years he lectured and studied without slackening, thoroughly mastering books on celestial offices, pitch pipes, and measures, and also studied from Huang Zongxi the arts of renchen escape and guxu divination.
translations.idiomatic: In prison there was a Fujianese man named Ke Zhongfu, an expert in astrology. Zhengzhong wished to study under him, citing how Huang Ba had learned the classics from Xiahou Sheng while imprisoned. For years he studied without cease, mastering works on celestial offices, pitch pipes, and measurement, and went on to learn from Huang Zongxi the techniques of renchen and guxu divination.

sentences.zh: 宗羲歎曰：「傳吾絕學者，仲撝一人耳！」

translations.literal: Zongxi sighed and said: "The one to transmit my lost learning is Zhongwei alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Zongxi sighed and said, "Of all who might carry on my lost learning, Zhongwei alone can do it!"

sentences.zh: 遂造監國魯元年丙戌大統歷以進。

translations.literal: He then compiled the Great Calendar for the first year of the Lu regency, bingxu, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He then compiled the Great Calendar for the first year of the Lu regency (bingxu) and submitted it to court.

sentences.zh: 浙東亡，避竄山中，貧不能自存，傍鑑湖佃田五畝，佐以醫卜自給。

translations.literal: When eastern Zhejiang fell, he hid in the mountains, too poor to sustain himself; he rented five mu of land beside Mirror Lake and supplemented his livelihood with medicine and divination.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern Zhejiang fell, he fled into the mountains. Too poor to live, he rented five mu beside Mirror Lake and supported himself with medicine and fortune-telling.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of the Kangxi reign, at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 著有周易註、律書詳註。

translations.literal: He authored Commentary on the Book of Changes and Detailed Commentary on the Treatise on Pitch Pipes.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include Commentary on the Book of Changes and Detailed Commentary on the Treatise on Pitch Pipes.

sentences.zh: 董守諭，字次公，鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Dong Shouyu, styled Cigong, was a native of Yin county.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shouyu, styled Cigong, was from Yin county.

sentences.zh: 舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 魯王監國，召為戶部貴州司主事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu governed as regent, he was summoned as chief clerk in the Guizhou Section of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu held the regency, Shouyu was summoned to serve as chief clerk in the Guizhou Section of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時熊汝霖、孫嘉績首事起兵，然皆書生，不知調度。

translations.literal: At the time Xiong Rulin and Sun Jiaji were the first to raise troops, but both were scholars and knew nothing of military logistics.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiong Rulin and Sun Jiaji had been first to raise troops, but both were bookish men with no knowledge of military supply.

sentences.zh: 乃迎方國安、王之仁，授之軍政，凡原設營兵、衛軍俱隸之。

translations.literal: They therefore welcomed Fang Guo'an and Wang Zhiren, entrusting them with military affairs; all formerly established camp troops and garrison forces were placed under their command.
translations.idiomatic: So they brought in Fang Guo'an and Wang Zhiren and placed military affairs in their hands—all existing camp soldiers and garrison troops fell under their command.

sentences.zh: 孫、熊所統，惟召募數百人。

translations.literal: What Sun and Xiong commanded amounted only to a few hundred recruited men.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and Xiong themselves commanded only a few hundred men they had recruited.

sentences.zh: 方、王兵既盛，反惡當國者有所參決，因而分餉分地之議起。

translations.literal: Once Fang's and Wang's forces had grown strong, they resented that those who governed had any say in decisions, and thus arose the debate over dividing rations and dividing territory.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fang's and Wang's armies had grown powerful, they resented any role for the court ministers in decision-making, and the disputes over dividing rations and assigning territories began.

sentences.zh: 分餉者，正兵食正餉，田賊之出也，方、王主之；

translations.literal: "Dividing rations" meant regular troops ate regular rations—revenue from land tax—and Fang and Wang would control this.
translations.idiomatic: "Dividing rations" meant regular troops would be paid from regular funds—land-tax revenue—and Fang and Wang would control that supply.

sentences.zh: 義兵食義餉，勸捐無名之徵也，熊、孫諸軍主之。

translations.literal: Volunteer troops ate volunteer rations—voluntary donations and unofficial levies—and Xiong, Sun, and their armies would control this.
translations.idiomatic: Volunteer troops would be paid from "volunteer funds"—donations and unofficial levies—and Xiong, Sun, and their forces would control those.

sentences.zh: 分地者，某正兵，支某邑正餉；

translations.literal: "Dividing territory" meant such-and-such regular troops would be paid from such-and-such a district's regular funds.
translations.idiomatic: "Dividing territory" meant assigning each regular unit its own district's tax revenue.

sentences.zh: 某義兵，支某邑義餉也。

translations.literal: Such-and-such volunteer troops would be paid from such-and-such a district's volunteer funds.
translations.idiomatic: Each volunteer unit would draw its pay from a designated district's donation pool.

sentences.zh: 魯王令廷臣集議，方、王司餉者，皆至殿陛譁爭，守諭曰：「諸君起義旅，咫尺天威，不守朝廷法乎？」

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu ordered court ministers to assemble for deliberation; Fang's and Wang's paymasters all came to the palace steps shouting in dispute. Shouyu said: "You gentlemen raised righteous armies—within a stone's throw of imperial majesty—will you not observe court law?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu convened the court to discuss the matter. The paymasters for Fang's and Wang's armies crowded the palace steps, shouting their claims. Shouyu said, "You raised armies to restore the dynasty—will you not obey the law within sight of the throne?"

sentences.zh: 乃稍退。

translations.literal: They then withdrew somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: At that they pulled back a little.

sentences.zh: 守諭又進曰：「義餉有名無實，以之饋義兵，必不繼。

translations.literal: Shouyu advanced again and said: "Volunteer funds exist in name but not in substance; using them to feed volunteer troops cannot be sustained.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyu pressed on: "Volunteer funds are mostly nominal. Pay volunteer troops from them and the supply will soon run dry.

sentences.zh: 即使能繼，誰為管庫？

translations.literal: Even if they could be sustained, who would manage the treasury?
translations.idiomatic: Even if they could be sustained, who would manage the stores?

sentences.zh: 今請以一切稅供悉歸戶部，計兵而後授餉，覈地之遠近，酌給之後先，則兵不絀於食，而餉可以時給也。」

translations.literal: I now ask that all tax revenue be returned entirely to the Ministry of Revenue; only after counting troops should rations be issued, weighing distance of territory and adjusting priority of payment—then troops will not lack food and rations can be issued on schedule."
translations.idiomatic: I propose placing all tax revenue under the Ministry of Revenue, allotting rations only after troops are counted, weighing distances between territories and setting priorities accordingly. Then the armies will never go hungry and pay will reach them on time."

sentences.zh: 方、王雖不從，然所議正，無以難也。

translations.literal: Fang and Wang did not assent, yet what he argued was correct and they could not refute it.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Wang did not agree, but they could find no fault with his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 之仁請收漁船稅，守諭曰：「今日所恃者人心耳，漁戶巳辦漁丁稅矣，若再苛求，民不堪命，人心一搖，國何以立？」

translations.literal: Zhiren requested to collect taxes on fishing boats. Shouyu said: "What we rely on today is the people's hearts. Fishing households already pay the fishing-boat levy—if we demand more, the people cannot bear it; once hearts waver, how can the state stand?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhiren wanted to levy a tax on fishing boats. Shouyu said, "Our foundation today is the people's loyalty. Fishing households already pay the boat tax—squeeze them further and they will break. Once hearts turn against us, how can this state endure?"

sentences.zh: 久之，又請行稅人法，請塞金錢湖為田，官賣大戶祀田贍軍，三疏皆下部議，兵士露刃以待覆，守諭力持不可。

translations.literal: After some time he again requested the "tax on persons" law, damming Gold Coin Lake to make fields and selling by government order the sacrificial fields of great families to support the army—three memorials all sent down for ministry deliberation. Soldiers bared their blades awaiting the reply; Shouyu firmly held they could not be approved.
translations.idiomatic: Later he pressed for a poll tax, for damming Gold Coin Lake into farmland, and for selling the sacrificial estates of great families to fund the army. All three proposals went to the ministries for review while soldiers waited with naked blades for approval. Shouyu held firm against every one.

sentences.zh: 之仁大怒，謂：「行朝大臣不敢裁量幕府，戶曹小臣敢爾阻大事邪？」

translations.literal: Zhiren flew into a rage and said: "Court ministers of the mobile government dare not restrain the military headquarters—a petty clerk of the revenue bureau dares thus to obstruct great affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhiren erupted in fury. "Court ministers won't stand up to the army," he said, "and this petty revenue clerk dares block my plans?"

sentences.zh: 檄召守諭，將殺之，魯王不能禁，令且避。

translations.literal: He issued an order summoning Shouyu, intending to kill him; the Prince of Lu could not forbid it and told Shouyu to withdraw for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a summons for Shouyu with intent to kill him. The Prince of Lu could not stop it and told Shouyu to withdraw for now.

sentences.zh: 守諭慷慨對曰：「司餉守正，臣分也。

translations.literal: Shouyu replied with bold spirit: "To manage rations and uphold what is right is my duty.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyu answered without flinching, "Managing rations and upholding what is right is my duty.

sentences.zh: 生殺出主上，武寧雖悍將，何為者？

translations.literal: Life and death belong to our sovereign; though the Prince of Wuning is a fierce general, what is he doing?
translations.idiomatic: The power of life and death rests with the sovereign. What business has the Prince of Wuning—a fierce general though he is—to decide it?

sentences.zh: 臣任死王前，聽武寧以臣血濺丹墀可耳！」

translations.literal: I accept death before the king; let the Prince of Wuning splash my blood upon the vermilion steps—that is all!"
translations.idiomatic: If I must die, let me die before the Prince. Let the Prince of Wuning splash my blood on the palace steps—that is all I ask!"

sentences.zh: 於是舉朝忿怒，曰：「之仁反邪，何敢無王命而害餉臣！」

translations.literal: At this the whole court was enraged and said: "Has Zhiren turned rebel? How dare he harm a paymaster without the king's command!"
translations.idiomatic: The whole court blazed with outrage: "Has Zhiren turned traitor? How dare he kill a paymaster without royal sanction!"

sentences.zh: 之仁乃止。

translations.literal: Zhiren then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiren backed down.

sentences.zh: 明年，莊烈帝大祥，守諭請謁朝堂哭，三軍縞素一日，遷經筵日講官，兼理餉事。

translations.literal: The next year, on the grand mourning for Emperor Zhuanglie, Shouyu requested to enter the court hall and weep; the three armies wore white mourning for a day; he was transferred to daily lecturer at the classics lecture, while also managing rations.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on the grand mourning for Emperor Zhuanglie, Shouyu petitioned to weep before the court. The entire army wore white for a day. He was promoted to daily lecturer at the classics lecture while continuing to manage rations.

sentences.zh: 魯王航海，守諭不及從，遂遯跡荒郊，旋卒。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu put to sea, Shouyu could not follow; he then hid in wild country and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu took to the sea, Shouyu could not follow. He vanished into the countryside and soon died.

sentences.zh: 著有攬蘭集。

translations.literal: He authored the Collection of Gathering Orchids.
translations.idiomatic: His Collection of Gathering Orchids survives.

sentences.zh: 陸宇，字周明，鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Lu Yu, styled Zhouming, was a native of Yin county.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yu, styled Zhouming, was from Yin county.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A student licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 慷慨尚氣節。

translations.literal: He was bold-spirited and honored integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and fiercely loyal to principle.

sentences.zh: 時有弟子訟其師，師不得直。

translations.literal: At the time a disciple brought suit against his teacher, and the teacher could obtain no justice.
translations.idiomatic: Once a student sued his teacher, and the courts would not give the teacher a fair hearing.

sentences.zh: 宇詣文廟，慟哭伐鼓，卒直其師而後止。

translations.literal: Yu went to the Confucian temple, wailed and beat the drum, and only when his teacher finally received justice did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: Yu went to the Confucian temple, wept bitterly, and beat the mourning drum until the courts finally gave his teacher justice.

sentences.zh: 明亡，嘗與黃宗羲謀舉事，其所與計畫者，皆四方知名士。

translations.literal: When the Ming fell, he once plotted rising with Huang Zongxi; those with whom he planned were all renowned men from every quarter.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Ming, he plotted rebellion with Huang Zongxi, drawing into their plans celebrated men from every corner of the realm.

sentences.zh: 其城西田舍，複壁柳車，雜賓死友。

translations.literal: At his farmstead west of the city, double walls and willow hearses concealed guests and friends wanted dead.
translations.idiomatic: At his farm west of the city he built hidden chambers and willow funeral carts to shelter fugitives and men marked for death.

sentences.zh: 計敗，喜事乃益甚。

translations.literal: When the plot failed, his zeal for righteous action only grew.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot failed, his zeal for the cause only burned brighter.

sentences.zh: 江湖間多傳其姓名，以為異人。

translations.literal: Throughout the rivers and lakes his name circulated widely, and people regarded him as an extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: His name traveled through the martial underworld, and many held him to be a man of singular gifts.

sentences.zh: 南都破，甬東師起，宇毀家紓餉。

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital fell, armies rose in eastern Yong; Yu ruined his family to ease the pay of troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing fell and armies rose in eastern Zhe, Yu liquidated his family fortune to help pay the troops.

sentences.zh: 翁洲又破，宇捐金與諜者，令訪死事消息。

translations.literal: When Weng Isle fell again, Yu gave gold to spies and had them inquire after news of those who had died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhoushan fell, Yu paid spies in gold to seek news of fallen comrades.

sentences.zh: 張肯堂之孫以俘至，亟治橐饘入獄視之，語其弟宇巇使為脫系。

translations.literal: The grandson of Zhang Huangyan arrived as a captive; Yu quickly prepared provisions in a bag and entered the prison to visit him, telling his younger brother Lu Xi to work for his release.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Huangyan's grandson arrived a prisoner, Yu hurriedly prepared food and entered the jail to see him, telling his brother Lu Xi to secure his release.

sentences.zh: 董志寧之喪在海上，宇致而葬之。

translations.literal: Dong Zhining's coffin was at sea; Yu brought it in and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhining's body lay unburied at sea; Yu recovered it and gave him proper burial.

sentences.zh: 旋為降卒所誣，捕入省獄，獄具，宇無所詿誤，脫械出門，未至館而卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was slandered by surrendered soldiers, seized and imprisoned in the provincial jail; when the case was closed Yu had implicated no one in error; shackles removed, he walked out the gate, and before reaching his lodging he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon surrendered soldiers framed him and he was thrown into the provincial jail. When the case closed he had implicated no innocent man. Shackles off, he walked out the gate—and died before reaching his lodging.

sentences.zh: 宇以好事盡其家產，室中所有，惟草薦敗絮及故書數百卷。

translations.literal: Yu had exhausted his family wealth in righteous causes; all his room held were straw mats, worn cotton, and several hundred old books.
translations.idiomatic: His zeal for the cause had consumed his entire fortune. His rooms held nothing but straw mats, worn rags, and a few hundred old books.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，家人整理其室，得布囊於亂書之下，發而視之，則赫然人頭也。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived, his family put his room in order and found a cloth sack beneath scattered books; opening it, they saw clearly—a human head.
translations.idiomatic: When news of his death reached home, his family tidied his room and found a cloth sack beneath a pile of books. They opened it—and there, plain as day, was a human head.

sentences.zh: 宇巇識其面目，捧之而泣曰：「此故少司馬篤庵王公頭也！」

translations.literal: Lu Xi recognized the face; he clasped it and wept, saying: "This is the head of the former Vice Minister of War, Lord Wang Du'an!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xi recognized the face. Clasping it, he wept and said, "This is the head of the late Vice Minister Wang Yi, styled Du'an!"

sentences.zh: 初，司馬兵敗，梟城闕，宇思收葬之，每徘徊其下。

translations.literal: At first when the Vice Minister's army was defeated, his head was displayed at the city gate; Yu thought to recover and bury it, and often lingered beneath it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang's army was defeated, his head was hung at the city gate. Yu had long hoped to recover it for burial and often lingered below.

sentences.zh: 一日，見暗中有叩首而去者，蹟之，走入破室。

translations.literal: One day he saw someone kowtowing in the shadows and leaving; he tracked the man, who ran into a ruined chamber.
translations.idiomatic: One day he saw a figure kowtowing in shadow and slipping away. He followed the man into a ruined hut.

sentences.zh: 宇曰：「子何人？」

translations.literal: Yu said: "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu asked, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 其人曰：「餘毛明山，曾以卒伍事司馬，今不勝故主之感耳！」

translations.literal: The man said: "I am Mao Mingshan. I once served the Vice Minister as a common soldier; I cannot bear my grief for my old master!"
translations.idiomatic: The man answered, "I am Mao Mingshan. I once served the Vice Minister as a common soldier—I cannot bear the grief for my old master!"

sentences.zh: 宇相與流涕，而詣江子云計所以收其頭者。

translations.literal: Yu wept with him and then went to Jiang Ziyun to plan how to recover the head.
translations.idiomatic: Yu wept with him, then went with him to Jiang Ziyun to plan the recovery of the head.

sentences.zh: 子云名漢，錢肅樂部將也。

translations.literal: Ziyun's given name was Han; he was a subordinate general under Qian Sule.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun, whose given name was Han, had been a subordinate general under Qian Sule.

sentences.zh: 失勢家居，會端陽競渡，遊人雜沓，子云紅笠握刀，從十餘人登城遨戲。

translations.literal: Having lost power he lived at home; on the Dragon Boat Festival boat races, when travelers crowded thickly, Ziyun wore a red hat, grasped a knife, and with a dozen-odd men climbed the wall to roam in sport.
translations.idiomatic: Out of office and living at home, he waited for the Dragon Boat Festival when the streets would throng with revelers. Ziyun put on a red hat, took up a knife, and with a dozen followers climbed the city wall as though out for sport.

sentences.zh: 至梟頭所，問守卒曰：「孰戴此頭也者？」

translations.literal: Reaching the place where the head was displayed, he asked the guarding soldier: "Whose head is hung here?"
translations.idiomatic: At the place where the head hung, he asked the guard, "Whose head is this?"

sentences.zh: 卒以司馬對。

translations.literal: The soldier answered that it was the Vice Minister's.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier said it was the Vice Minister's.

sentences.zh: 子云佯怒曰：「嘻！

translations.literal: Ziyun feigned anger and said: "Ha!
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun feigned rage. "Ha!

sentences.zh: 吾怨家也，亦有是日乎？」

translations.literal: He is my sworn enemy—has his day come at last?"
translations.idiomatic: My sworn enemy—and I live to see this day?"

sentences.zh: 拔刀擊之，繩斷墮地，宇、明山已豫立城下。

translations.literal: He drew his knife and struck; the rope snapped and the head fell; Yu and Mingshan were already standing ready below the wall.
translations.idiomatic: He slashed with his knife. The rope snapped and the head fell. Below the wall Yu and Mingshan were already waiting.

sentences.zh: 方是時，龍舟噪甚，人無回面易視者，宇以身蔽，明山拾頭雜儔人而去。

translations.literal: At that moment the dragon boats were very noisy; no one turned to look easily; Yu sheltered with his body while Mingshan picked up the head and mingled with the crowd and left.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon boats roared; no one turned to stare. Yu shielded the scene with his body while Mingshan snatched up the head and melted into the crowd.

sentences.zh: 宇祀之書室，蓋十二年矣，而家人無知者。

translations.literal: Yu enshrined it in his study—for twelve years—and his family knew nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had kept it enshrined in his study for twelve years, and not one person in his household knew.

sentences.zh: 至是宇巇始瘞之。

translations.literal: Only now did Lu Xi at last bury it.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Lu Xi finally bury it.

sentences.zh: 宇巇，宇第五弟，字春明。

translations.literal: Lu Xi was Yu's fifth younger brother, styled Chunming.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xi was Yu's fifth younger brother, styled Chunming.

sentences.zh: 負才自喜，俯視一切。

translations.literal: He trusted in his talent and looked down on everything.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his gifts, he looked down on the world.

sentences.zh: 宇風格棱棱不可犯，而宇巇稍濟之以和，故世人親之如夏日冬日之分。

translations.literal: Yu's bearing was sharp and unapproachable, while Lu Xi slightly tempered it with gentleness; thus people felt close to them as to summer and winter respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's manner was austere and forbidding; Lu Xi softened it with warmth. People drew near to them as they do to summer and winter in turn.

sentences.zh: 然其刻意勵行，雖嚬笑皆歸名節，則一也。

translations.literal: Yet in deliberately cultivating conduct, even frown and smile were subordinated to moral integrity—the same for both.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both cultivated their conduct with deliberate rigor: even a smile or frown served principle. In that they were one.

sentences.zh: 丙戌後，棄諸生與諸遺民遊，荒亭木末，時聞野哭。

translations.literal: After bingxu he abandoned his licentiate status and wandered with other loyalist recluses; at ruined pavilions and treetops one could sometimes hear wild weeping.
translations.idiomatic: After 1646 he gave up his licentiate standing and wandered with fellow loyalists among ruined pavilions and treetops, where sometimes one heard the wild wailing of mourners.

sentences.zh: 同里秀才杜懋俊，仗義死難，藏其遺孤。

translations.literal: Du Maojun, a licentiate of his village, had died nobly for the cause; Lu Xi hid his orphaned child.
translations.idiomatic: Du Maojun, a licentiate from his home village, had died for the cause. Lu Xi sheltered his orphaned child.

sentences.zh: 桐城方授，避地來鄞，宇巇館之湖樓中。

translations.literal: Fang Shou of Tongcheng, seeking refuge, came to Yin; Lu Xi lodged him in a lakeside tower.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Shou of Tongcheng fled to Yin county, and Lu Xi housed him in a lakeside pavilion.

sentences.zh: 授卒，宇巇經紀其喪，收拾遺文以致其家。

translations.literal: When Shou died, Lu Xi managed his funeral, gathered his remaining writings, and sent them to his family.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Shou died, Lu Xi arranged his funeral, gathered his surviving writings, and sent them home to his family.

sentences.zh: 性嗜異書，晚年，家既貧，不能具寫官，乃手鈔之，瀕病不倦。

translations.literal: By nature he loved rare books; in his old age, his family already poor, unable to hire copyists, he copied them by hand and did not tire even when near death.
translations.idiomatic: He loved rare books passionately. In old age, too poor to hire copyists, he transcribed them by hand, laboring on even as illness closed in.

sentences.zh: 從子官山左，令其訪東萊趙士喆遺書，垂歿，尚以其書未至為恨。

translations.literal: His nephew served as official in eastern Shandong; Lu Xi had him seek out the surviving writings of Zhao Shizhe of Donglai, and on the verge of death still grieved that the books had not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew held office in Shandong; Lu Xi sent him to find the surviving works of Zhao Shizhe of Donglai. On his deathbed he still mourned that the books had not reached him.

sentences.zh: 自棄諸生，即練衣蔬食，叢林以為佞佛，爭勸之披緇，宇巇笑不答。

translations.literal: From the time he abandoned his licentiate status he wore plain hemp and ate vegetables; Buddhist clergy thought him devout and all urged him to take the tonsure; Lu Xi smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he renounced his licentiate status he wore coarse cloth and ate plain food. Buddhist clergy took him for a devotee and urged him to enter the priesthood. Lu Xi only smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 及遺命不作佛事，眾始瞿然。

translations.literal: When his dying instructions forbade Buddhist rites, the crowd at last started in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: When his will forbade Buddhist funeral rites, everyone was startled into new respect.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 著觀日堂集八卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Collected Works of the Hall for Contemplating the Sun in eight fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: His Collected Works of the Hall for Contemplating the Sun survives in eight fascicles.

sentences.zh: 漢，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Han was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Han was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 為肅樂所倚恃，授以都督僉事總兵官。

translations.literal: Qian Sule relied on him and appointed him Vice Commissioner-in-chief and supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Sule trusted him and made him Vice Commissioner-in-chief and supreme regional commander.

sentences.zh: 師至閩，幾下福州，漢功為多。

translations.literal: When the army reached Fujian and nearly took Fuzhou, Han's achievements were greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched into Fujian and nearly captured Fuzhou, Han's merit was greatest among them.

sentences.zh: 侍郎馮景第之乞師日本也，請與偕行。

translations.literal: When Vice Minister Feng Jingdi petitioned to seek troops from Japan, Han asked to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister Feng Jingdi petitioned to seek aid from Japan, Han asked to accompany the mission.

sentences.zh: 及歸，漢曰：「東師必不出也！」

translations.literal: When they returned, Han said: "Eastern troops will certainly not come out!"
translations.idiomatic: On their return Han said, "The Japanese will never send troops!"

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: Before long it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was proved right.

sentences.zh: 肅樂既卒，漢侍母居鄞，種蔬自給，四壁無長物，惟餘肅樂所贈寶刀一而已。

translations.literal: After Sule died, Han served his mother and lived at Yin, growing vegetables to support himself; the four walls had nothing of length—only the precious saber Sule had given him remained.
translations.idiomatic: After Sule's death Han cared for his mother in Yin county, supporting them by growing vegetables. His bare rooms held nothing but the treasured saber Sule had given him.

sentences.zh: 每語及肅樂，則淚淋淋下，抑鬱終。

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke of Sule, tears streamed down; he died in melancholy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke of Sule, tears streamed down his face. He died of sorrow.

sentences.zh: 方以智，字密之，桐城人。

translations.literal: Fang Yizhi, styled Mizhi, was a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yizhi, styled Mizhi, was from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 父孔炤，明湖廣巡撫，為楊嗣昌劾下獄，以智懷血疏訟冤，得釋，事具明史。

translations.literal: His father Kong Zhao was Ming governor-general of Huguang; impeached by Yang Sichang and imprisoned, Yizhi submitted a blood petition to plead his innocence and secured his release—the affair is fully recorded in the Ming History.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kong Zhao had served the Ming as governor-general of Huguang. When Yang Sichang impeached him and had him thrown into prison, Yizhi submitted a blood petition to plead his innocence and won his release; the affair is fully recorded in the Ming History.

sentences.zh: 以智，崇禎庚辰進士，授檢討。

translations.literal: Yizhi became a jinshi in the gengchen year of Chongzhen and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi passed the jinshi examination in the gengchen year of Chongzhen and was appointed a Hanlin reviser.

sentences.zh: 會李自成破潼關，範景文疏薦以智，召對德政殿，語中機要，上撫幾稱善。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng broke through Tong Pass, Fan Jingwen memorialized recommending Yizhi; summoned for audience in Dezheng Hall, his words hit the vital points, and the emperor stroked the armrest and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng broke through Tong Pass, Fan Jingwen recommended Yizhi in a memorial. Summoned to audience in Dezheng Hall, he spoke to the heart of the crisis, and the emperor stroked the armrest and praised him.

sentences.zh: 以忤執政意，不果用。

translations.literal: Because he offended the ruling faction's wishes, he was not in the end employed.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had offended those in power, he was never given office.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，以智哭臨殯宮，至東華門，被執，加刑毒，兩髁骨見，不屈。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Yizhi went to wail at the mourning palace; reaching Donghua Gate he was seized, subjected to cruel torture until both kneecaps were laid bare, yet he did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Yizhi went to mourn at the imperial mourning hall. At Donghua Gate he was seized and tortured until both kneecaps were laid bare, yet he would not submit.

sentences.zh: 賊敗，南奔，值馬、阮亂政，修怨欲殺之，遂流離嶺表。

translations.literal: When the rebels were defeated he fled south; encountering the disorderly rule of Ma and Ruan, who nursed old grudges and wished to kill him, he then wandered destitute in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated he fled south. Ma Shiying and Ruan Dacheng were ruining the government and, nursing old grudges, sought his life, so he wandered destitute through Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 自作序篇，上述祖德，下表隱志。

translations.literal: He himself composed a prefatory account, above setting forth ancestral virtue, below declaring his hidden resolve.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a prefatory account of his own life, praising his ancestors above and declaring his resolve to live in seclusion below.

sentences.zh: 變姓名，賣藥市中。

translations.literal: He changed his name and sold medicine in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his name and sold medicine in the market towns.

sentences.zh: 桂王稱號肇慶，以與推戴功，擢右中允。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Gui assumed his title at Zhaoqing, for his merit in supporting the enthronement he was promoted to right palace aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Gui took the throne at Zhaoqing, Yizhi was promoted to right palace aide for his role in supporting the enthronement.

sentences.zh: 扈王幸梧州，擢侍講學士，拜禮部侍郎、東閣大學士，旋罷相。

translations.literal: Escorting the prince to Wuzhou, he was promoted reader-in-waiting, appointed Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, and soon dismissed from the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the prince to Wuzhou, he was made reader-in-waiting, then Vice Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion—only to be dismissed from the chancellorship soon after.

sentences.zh: 固稱疾，屢詔不起。

translations.literal: He firmly pleaded illness and repeatedly ignored imperial summons.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly pleaded illness and repeatedly refused the emperor's summons.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾歸則負君，出則負親，吾其緇乎？」

translations.literal: He once said: "If I return, I fail my sovereign; if I go forth, I fail my parents—shall I take the tonsure?"
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "If I go back, I betray my sovereign; if I go out, I betray my parents—shall I take the tonsure?"

sentences.zh: 行至平樂，被縶。

translations.literal: Traveling to Pingle, he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: On the road to Pingle he was seized.

sentences.zh: 其帥欲降之，左置官服，右白刃，惟所擇，以智趨右，帥更加禮敬，始聽為僧。

translations.literal: The commander wished to win him over; on the left official robes were set out, on the right a naked blade—he might choose as he pleased. Yizhi moved toward the right; the commander showed him even greater courtesy and only then permitted him to become a monk.
translations.idiomatic: The commander tried to win him over, setting official robes on the left and a naked blade on the right for him to choose. Yizhi moved toward the blade. The commander treated him with even greater respect and only then allowed him to become a monk.

sentences.zh: 更名弘智，字無可，別號藥地。

translations.literal: He changed his name to Hongzhi, styled Wuke, with the sobriquet Yaodi.
translations.idiomatic: He took the monastic name Hongzhi, styled Wuke, and the sobriquet Yaodi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，赴吉安，拜文信國墓，道卒，其閉關高座時也。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi he went to Ji'an to pay respects at the tomb of Wen, Duke of Xinguo, and died on the road—this was during his period of seclusion in meditation.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kangxi he set out for Ji'an to pay his respects at the tomb of Wen, Duke of Xinguo, and died on the road, still in the midst of his meditative seclusion.

sentences.zh: 友人錢澄之，亦客金陵，遇故中官為僧者，問以智，澄之曰：「君豈曾識耶？」

translations.literal: His friend Qian Chengshi was also staying in Jinling when he met a former palace eunuch who had become a monk; asked about Yizhi, Chengshi said: "Did you ever know him?"
translations.idiomatic: His friend Qian Chengshi was also staying in Jinling when he met a former palace eunuch turned monk. Asked about Yizhi, Chengshi said, "Did you ever know him?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「非也。

translations.literal: He said: "No.
translations.idiomatic: The monk said, "No.

sentences.zh: 昔侍先皇，一日朝罷，上忽歎曰：'求忠臣必於孝子！

translations.literal: In former days I attended the late emperor; one day after court was dismissed the emperor suddenly sighed and said: 'Seek loyal ministers among filial sons!'
translations.idiomatic: Long ago I served the late emperor. One day after court was dismissed the emperor suddenly sighed and said, 'Seek loyal ministers among filial sons!'

sentences.zh: '如是者再。

translations.literal: Thus he spoke twice.
translations.idiomatic: He said it twice.

sentences.zh: 某跪請故，上曰：'早禦經筵，有講官父巡撫河南，坐失機問大辟，某薰衣，飾容止如常時。

translations.literal: I knelt and asked the reason; the emperor said: 'Earlier at the Classics lecture, there was a lecturer whose father was governor of Henan and faced execution for military failure; he perfumed his robes and composed his bearing as at ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: I knelt and asked why. The emperor said, 'Earlier at the Classics lecture there was a lecturer whose father, governor of Henan, faced execution for military failure. He perfumed his robes and carried himself as if nothing were wrong.

sentences.zh: 不孝若此，能為忠乎？

translations.literal: So unfilial as this—can he be loyal?
translations.idiomatic: So unfilial—how could he be loyal?

sentences.zh: 聞新進士方以智，父亦繫獄，日號泣，持疏求救，此亦人子也。

translations.literal: I hear the newly minted jinshi Fang Yizhi also has a father imprisoned; day after day he wails and submits memorials begging rescue—this too is a son.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the new jinshi Fang Yizhi also has a father in prison. Day after day he weeps and submits memorials begging for rescue. That too is a son.

sentences.zh: '言訖复嘆，俄釋孔炤，而辟河南巡撫，外廷亦知其故乎？」

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking he sighed again; soon Kong Zhao was released, while the Henan governor was executed—does the outer court also know the reason?'"
translations.idiomatic: When he finished he sighed again. Soon Kong Zhao was released and the Henan governor was executed. Does the outer court know why?'"

sentences.zh: 澄之述其語告以智，以智伏地哭失聲。

translations.literal: Chengshi repeated these words and told Yizhi; Yizhi prostrated himself and wept aloud beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi repeated the story to Yizhi, who fell prostrate and wept uncontrollably.

sentences.zh: 以智生有異禀，年十五，群經、子、史，略能背誦。

translations.literal: Yizhi was born with unusual gifts; at fifteen he could largely recite from memory the Classics, Masters, and Histories.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi was born with unusual gifts. By fifteen he could recite from memory most of the Classics, Masters, and Histories.

sentences.zh: 博涉多通，自天文、輿地、禮樂、律數、聲音、文字、書畫、醫藥、技勇之屬，皆能考其源流，析其旨趣。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and widely accomplished, from astronomy, geography, ritual and music, pitch and number, sound, writing, painting and calligraphy, medicine, and martial skill—he could trace the origins and currents of them all and analyze their essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: His learning was broad and his mastery wide. In astronomy, geography, ritual and music, pitch and number, phonology, writing, painting and calligraphy, medicine, and martial arts alike, he could trace origins and currents and analyze their essential meaning.

sentences.zh: 著書數十萬言，惟通雅、物理小識二書盛行於世。

translations.literal: He authored several hundred thousand characters of books; only Tongya and Wuli Xiaoshi circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote several hundred thousand characters of books, but only Tongya and Wuli Xiaoshi achieved wide circulation.

sentences.zh: 子中德，字田伯，著古事比。

translations.literal: His son Zhongde, styled Tianbo, authored Gu Shibi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongde, styled Tianbo, wrote Gu Shibi.

sentences.zh: 以智構馬、阮之難，中德年十三，撾登聞鼓，訟父冤。

translations.literal: When Yizhi fell into trouble with Ma and Ruan, Zhongde at thirteen beat the Gate of Imperial Complaint drum to plead his father's injustice.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhi fell afoul of Ma Shiying and Ruan Dacheng, thirteen-year-old Zhongde beat the Gate of Imperial Complaint drum to plead his father's innocence.

sentences.zh: 父出亡，偕諸弟徒步追從。

translations.literal: When his father fled into exile, he joined his younger brothers in following on foot.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fled into exile, he and his younger brothers followed on foot.

sentences.zh: 中通，字位伯，精算術，著數度衍，見疇人傳。

translations.literal: Zhongtong, styled Weibo, was skilled in calculation; he authored Shudu Yan and appears in the Biographies of Calendar Experts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongtong, styled Weibo, was skilled in mathematics. He wrote Shudu Yan and is treated in the Biographies of Calendar Experts.

sentences.zh: 中屨，字素伯，幼隨父於方外，備嘗險阻，著古今釋疑。

translations.literal: Zhonglu, styled Subo, from youth followed his father in the religious life, tasted every hardship and danger, and authored Gujin Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglu, styled Subo, followed his father into monastic life from childhood, endured every hardship, and wrote Gujin Shiyi.

sentences.zh: 錢澄之，字飲光，原名秉鐙，桐城人。

translations.literal: Qian Chengshi, styled Yinguang, original name Bingdeng, was a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chengshi, styled Yinguang and originally named Bingdeng, was from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 少以名節自勵。

translations.literal: From youth he took reputation and integrity as his discipline.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he held himself to the standards of honor and integrity.

sentences.zh: 有御史巡按至皖，盛儀從，謁孔子廟，諸生迎迓門外。

translations.literal: When a censor arrived on provincial inspection in Anhui with a grand retinue to visit the Confucian temple, the students welcomed him outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When a touring censor arrived in Anhui with a grand retinue to visit the Confucian temple, the students lined up outside the gate to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 澄之忽前扳車，御史大駭，止車，因抗聲數其穢行。

translations.literal: Chengshi suddenly stepped forward and seized the carriage; the censor was greatly alarmed and halted, whereupon Chengshi raised his voice and enumerated his foul conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi suddenly stepped forward and seized the carriage. The censor was alarmed and stopped. Chengshi then raised his voice and publicly denounced his foul conduct.

sentences.zh: 御史故閹黨，方自幸脫「逆案」，內懼不敢究其事。

translations.literal: The censor was a former eunuch-faction man who had just congratulated himself on escaping the "treason case"; inwardly afraid, he did not dare pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The censor was a former member of the eunuch faction who had only just congratulated himself on escaping "the treason case." Too frightened to press the matter, he let it drop.

sentences.zh: 澄之以此名聞。

translations.literal: Chengshi became famous for this.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi won fame for this act.

sentences.zh: 是時復社、幾社始興，比郡中主壇坫者，宣城沈壽民，池陽吳應箕，桐城則澄之及方以智，而澄之又與陳子龍、夏允彝輩聯雲龍社，以接武東林。

translations.literal: At that time Fushe and Jishe were just rising; in neighboring commanderies those who presided over the literary altars were Shen Shoumin of Xuancheng and Wu Yingji of Chiyang; in Tongcheng, Chengshi and Fang Yizhi—and Chengshi also joined Chen Zilong, Xia Yunyi, and others in the Yunlong Society, taking up the mantle of the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fushe and Jishe were just rising. In neighboring prefectures Shen Shoumin of Xuancheng and Wu Yingji of Chiyang presided over the literary societies; in Tongcheng it was Chengshi and Fang Yizhi. Chengshi also joined Chen Zilong, Xia Yunyi, and others in the Yunlong Society, carrying on the tradition of the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 澄之體貌偉然，好飲酒，縱談經世之略。

translations.literal: Chengshi was imposing in build, loved wine, and discoursed freely on statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi was imposing in stature, fond of wine, and given to free talk of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 嘗思冒危難，立功名。

translations.literal: He once thought to brave danger and establish merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: He long dreamed of braving danger to win merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 阮大鋮既柄用，刊章捕治黨人，澄之先避吳中，妻方赴水死，事具明史。

translations.literal: Once Ruan Dacheng seized power and published edicts to arrest and punish faction members, Chengshi fled first to Wu; his wife Fang drowned herself—the affair is fully recorded in the Ming History.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruan Dacheng seized power and issued edicts to arrest faction members, Chengshi fled to Wu first. His wife Fang drowned herself; the affair is fully recorded in the Ming History.

sentences.zh: 於是亡命走浙、閩，入粵，崎嶇險絕，猶數從鋒鏑間支持名義不少屈。

translations.literal: He then fled for his life through Zhejiang and Fujian into Guangdong; over paths rugged beyond measure he still repeatedly upheld righteous principle amid clashing blades and did not yield in the least.
translations.idiomatic: He then fled through Zhejiang and Fujian into Guangdong. Over paths rugged beyond measure he still repeatedly upheld the loyalist cause amid clashing blades and never yielded.

sentences.zh: 黃道周薦諸唐王，授吉安府推官，改延平府。

translations.literal: Huang Daozhou recommended him to the Prince of Tang, and he was appointed investigating censor of Ji'an Prefecture, then transferred to Yanping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou recommended him to the Prince of Tang, and he was appointed investigating censor of Ji'an Prefecture, then transferred to Yanping.

sentences.zh: 桂王時，擢禮部主事，特試，授翰林院庶吉士，兼誥敕撰文。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Gui he was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Rites; by special examination he was made a Hanlin bachelor and also charged with drafting imperial patents and edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Gui he was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Rites. By special examination he became a Hanlin bachelor and was also charged with drafting patents and edicts.

sentences.zh: 指陳皆切時弊，忌者眾，乃乞假，間道歸里。

translations.literal: His recommendations all cut to present abuses; those who resented him were many, so he requested leave and returned home by secret routes.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials cut to the heart of the abuses of the day. Resentment against him was widespread, so he requested leave and returned home by secret routes.

sentences.zh: 結廬先人墓旁，環廬皆田也，自號曰田間，著田間詩學、易學。

translations.literal: He built a hut beside his forebears' tomb; fields surrounded the hut on every side, and he styled himself Tianjian, authoring Tianjian Studies of Poetry and the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut beside his ancestors' tomb, with fields all around, and styled himself Tianjian. He wrote Tianjian Studies of Poetry and the Changes.

sentences.zh: 澄之嘗問易道周，依京房、邵雍說，究極數學，後乃兼求義理。

translations.literal: Chengshi once studied the Changes under Daozhou, following the teachings of Jing Fang and Shao Yong to pursue mathematics to its limits, and later also sought moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi once studied the Changes under Huang Daozhou, following Jing Fang and Shao Yong to pursue numerical cosmology to its limits, and later also sought moral principle.

sentences.zh: 其治詩，遵用小序首句，於名物、訓詁、山川、地理尤詳。

translations.literal: In his treatment of the Odes he followed the opening lines of the Small Prefaces, and was especially detailed on names and things, glosses, mountains and rivers, and geography.
translations.idiomatic: In his work on the Odes he followed the opening lines of the Small Prefaces and was especially detailed on names and things, glosses, and geography.

sentences.zh: 自謂著易、詩成，思所以翊二經者，而得莊周、屈原，乃復著莊屈合詁。

translations.literal: He said that once his works on the Changes and the Odes were complete, thinking how to support the two Classics he turned to Zhuang Zhou and Qu Yuan, and then also authored Combined Glosses on Zhuangzi and Qu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Once his works on the Changes and the Odes were complete, he sought further ways to support those two Classics and turned to Zhuangzi and Qu Yuan, writing Combined Glosses on Zhuangzi and Qu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 蓋澄之生值末季，離憂抑鬱無所洩，一寓之於言，故以莊繼易，以屈繼詩也。

translations.literal: For Chengshi was born in the final age; parting and sorrow, depression with no outlet—all were poured into words, hence Zhuangzi followed the Changes and Qu Yuan followed the Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi was born in the dynasty's final age. Parting, sorrow, and depression with no outlet he poured into words—hence Zhuangzi after the Changes and Qu Yuan after the Odes.

sentences.zh: 又有藏山閣詩文集。

translations.literal: He also had the Cangshange Collection of poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: He also left the Cangshange Collection of poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 惲日初，字仲升，號遜菴，武進人。

translations.literal: Yun Richu, styled Zhongsheng, sobriquet Sun'an, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Richu, styled Zhongsheng and known as Sun'an, was from Wujin.

sentences.zh: 崇禎癸酉副榜。

translations.literal: In the guiyou year of Chongzhen he placed on the second list of the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He placed on the second list of the provincial examination in the guiyou year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 久留京師，應詔上備邊五策，不報。

translations.literal: Long resident in the capital, in response to an imperial edict he submitted five strategies for frontier defense; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: He remained long in the capital and, responding to an imperial edict, submitted five strategies for frontier defense, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 知時事不可為，乃歸隱天台山。

translations.literal: Knowing the times could not be set right, he retired to seclusion on Mount Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the times could not be set right, he withdrew to seclusion on Mount Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 兩京亡，唐王立福州，魯王亦監國紹興，吏部侍郎姜垓薦日初知兵，魯王遣使聘之，固辭不起。
