translations.literal: When both capitals fell, the Prince of Tang established his rule at Fuzhou and the Prince of Lu also governed from Shaoxing; Vice Minister of Personnel Jiang Gai recommended Richu as knowing warfare; the Prince of Lu sent envoys to engage him, but he firmly declined and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When both capitals fell, the Prince of Tang established his court at Fuzhou and the Prince of Lu governed from Shaoxing. Vice Minister Jiang Gai recommended Richu as a military expert. The Prince of Lu sent envoys to engage him, but he steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 大兵下浙，避走福州；

translations.literal: When the great army descended on Zhejiang, he fled to Fuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: When the great army descended on Zhejiang, he fled to Fuzhou;

sentences.zh: 福州破，走廣州；

translations.literal: when Fuzhou fell, he fled to Guangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: when Fuzhou fell, he fled to Guangzhou;

sentences.zh: 廣州复破，乃祝髮為浮圖，復至建陽。

translations.literal: when Guangzhou also fell, he tonsured his head and became a Buddhist monk, then returned to Jianyang.
translations.idiomatic: when Guangzhou also fell, he tonsured his head and became a monk, then made his way back to Jianyang.

sentences.zh: 是時唐王被執死，魯王亦敗走海外，湖廣何騰蛟、江西楊廷麟等皆前後覆滅，而明遺臣尚擁殘旅，遙奉永曆。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Tang was captured and killed, the Prince of Lu also defeated and fled overseas, He Tengjiao of Huguang and Yang Tinglin of Jiangxi were all destroyed one after another, yet Ming loyalists still held remnant forces and from afar upheld Yongli.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Prince of Tang had been captured and killed and the Prince of Lu defeated and driven overseas. He Tengjiao in Huguang and Yang Tinglin in Jiangxi had fallen in turn, yet Ming loyalists still held remnant forces and from afar upheld the Yongli regime.

sentences.zh: 金壇人王祈聚眾入建寧，屬縣多響應。

translations.literal: Wang Qi of Jintan gathered a host and entered Jianning; many subordinate counties responded in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qi of Jintan raised a force and entered Jianning, and many neighboring counties answered his call.

sentences.zh: 日初曰：「建寧，入閩門戶，能守，則諸郡安，然不扼仙霞關，建寧終不守也。

translations.literal: Richu said: "Jianning is the gateway into Fujian; if it can be held, the commanderies will be secure—yet unless Xianxia Pass is seized, Jianning in the end cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: Richu said, "Jianning is the gateway into Fujian. Hold it and the prefectures will be secure—but unless Xianxia Pass is seized, Jianning cannot be held in the end.

sentences.zh: 欲取仙霞，宜先取蒲城。」

translations.literal: To take Xianxia, one should first take Pucheng."
translations.idiomatic: To take Xianxia, one must first take Pucheng."

sentences.zh: 乃遣長子楨隨副將謝南雲先趨蒲城，失利，皆死。

translations.literal: He then sent his eldest son Zhen with Vice General Xie Nanyun to hurry first to Pucheng; they met defeat and both died.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his eldest son Zhen with Vice General Xie Nanyun to strike first at Pucheng. They were defeated and both died.

sentences.zh: 而御史徐云兵連入數州縣，銳甚，日初說令夜入蒲城，自督兵繼進。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Censor Xu Yun's troops pressed in succession into several prefectures and counties, very sharp in momentum; Richu persuaded him to enter Pucheng by night while Richu himself led troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Censor Xu Yun's troops swept through several prefectures and counties with great momentum. Richu persuaded him to enter Pucheng by night while he himself led troops in support.

sentences.zh: 會大雷雨，人馬衝泥淖，行不能速，軍遂潰。

translations.literal: A great thunderstorm came; men and horses churned through mud and mire and could not advance quickly, and the army then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: A great thunderstorm struck. Men and horses bogged down in mud and could not advance quickly, and the army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 建寧被圍，王使兵部尚書揭重熙赴援。

translations.literal: Jianning was besieged; Wang sent Minister of War Jie Chongxi to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianning was besieged, Wang sent Minister of War Jie Chongxi to its relief.

sentences.zh: 日初上書，請迳取蒲城，斷仙霞嶺餉道，徐與圍中諸將夾擊之。

translations.literal: Richu submitted a memorial requesting to strike directly at Pucheng, cut the supply route over Xianxia Ridge, and then join the besieged generals in a pincer attack.
translations.idiomatic: Richu submitted a memorial urging a direct strike at Pucheng to cut the supply route over Xianxia Ridge, then join the besieged generals in a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 重熙巡至邵武，不能進，建寧遂破，王祈力戰死。

translations.literal: Chongxi toured as far as Shaowu and could not advance; Jianning then fell, and Wang Qi died fighting to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxi advanced only as far as Shaowu and could go no farther. Jianning fell, and Wang Qi died fighting to the end.

sentences.zh: 日初收殘卒走廣信，尋入封禁山中，數日糧盡，喟然曰：「天下事壞散已數十年，不可救正。

translations.literal: Richu gathered remnant troops and fled to Guangxin, then entered the Fengjin Mountains; after several days provisions were exhausted, and he sighed and said: "The affairs of the realm have been ruined and scattered for decades already—they cannot be set right.
translations.idiomatic: Richu gathered remnant troops and fled to Guangxin, then withdrew into the Fengjin Mountains. After several days their provisions ran out, and he sighed and said, "The affairs of the realm have been ruined and scattered for decades—they cannot be set right.

sentences.zh: 然莊烈帝殉社稷，薄海茹痛，小臣愚妄，謂即此可延天命。

translations.literal: Yet the Zhuanglie Emperor died for the altars of state; all within the seas gnawed with grief; this petty subject in foolish presumption thought that by this alone the Mandate of Heaven might be prolonged.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Zhuanglie Emperor died for the altars of state, and grief gnawed at every corner of the realm. In foolish presumption this petty subject thought that even so the Mandate might yet be prolonged.

sentences.zh: 今乃至此，徒毒百姓，何益？」

translations.literal: Now it has come to this—only to poison the common people; what good is there in it?"
translations.idiomatic: Now it has come to this, poisoning the common people to no purpose. What good is there in it?"

sentences.zh: 遂散眾，獨行歸常州。

translations.literal: He then dismissed his followers and returned alone to Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then dismissed his followers and returned alone to Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，張煌言與鄭成功軍薄江寧，敗走。

translations.literal: After a long interval, the armies of Zhang Huangyan and Zheng Chenggong pressed close to Jiangning and were defeated and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the armies of Zhang Huangyan and Zheng Chenggong pressed close to Jiangning and were defeated and driven off.

sentences.zh: 訛傳張弟鳳翼乃日初門人，從師匿，縣官將收捕，日初色如常，曰：「吾當死久矣。」

translations.literal: A false report spread that Zhang's younger brother Fengyi was Richu's disciple and was hiding with his teacher; the county magistrate was about to arrest him. Richu's countenance was as usual, and he said: "I ought to have died long ago."
translations.idiomatic: A false report spread that Zhang's younger brother Fengyi was Richu's disciple and was hiding with him. When the county magistrate moved to arrest him, Richu's face showed no change. He said, "I ought to have died long ago."

sentences.zh: 既而事解。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the affair was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the matter was resolved.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十有八。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 少與楊廷樞等交，於百氏無所不窺，尤喜宋儒書。

translations.literal: From youth he associated with Yang Tingji and others; of the hundred schools there was none he did not investigate, and he especially loved the books of Song Neo-Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he associated with Yang Tingji and others. There was scarcely a school of thought he did not explore, and he especially loved the Song Neo-Confucians.

sentences.zh: 及從劉宗周遊，學益進，嘗上書申

translations.literal: After traveling with Liu Zongzhou his learning advanced further; he once submitted a memorial to plead for
translations.idiomatic: After traveling with Liu Zongzhou his learning advanced further, and he once submitted a memorial pleading for

sentences.zh: 救，義聲震天下。

translations.literal: rescue, and his righteous reputation shook the whole realm.
translations.idiomatic: his rescue, and his righteous fame resounded throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 丙戌後，累至山陰哭祭，為之行狀，近十萬言。

translations.literal: After the bingxu year he repeatedly went to Shanyin to mourn and offer sacrifice, and composed a biographical account of nearly one hundred thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: After the bingxu year he repeatedly went to Shanyin to mourn and offer sacrifice, and wrote a biographical account of nearly one hundred thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 晚服浮圖服，而言學者多宗之。

translations.literal: In later years he wore Buddhist robes, and many who spoke of learning took him as their master.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he wore Buddhist robes, and many scholars looked to him as their master.

sentences.zh: 無錫高世泰重葺東林書院，日初與同志習禮其間。

translations.literal: Gao Shitai of Wuxi rebuilt the Donglin Academy; Richu and like-minded men practiced ritual there.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shitai of Wuxi rebuilt the Donglin Academy, and Richu practiced ritual there with like-minded companions.

sentences.zh: 知常州府駱鍾泰屢求見，不納。

translations.literal: Lu Zhongtai, prefect of Changzhou, repeatedly sought an audience and was not received.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhongtai, prefect of Changzhou, repeatedly sought an audience, but Richu would not receive him.

sentences.zh: 去官後，與一見，言中庸要領，喜而去，曰：「不圖今日得聆大儒緒論也！」

translations.literal: After leaving office he granted one meeting; speaking on the essentials of the Doctrine of the Mean, Lu went away pleased and said: "I never thought that today I could hear a great scholar's foundational discourse!"
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office Richu granted him one meeting. Speaking on the essentials of the Doctrine of the Mean, Lu went away delighted and said, "I never dreamed that today I would hear a great scholar's foundational discourse!"

sentences.zh: 次子桓，在建寧被掠，不知所終；

translations.literal: His second son Huan was captured at Jianning; his end is unknown;
translations.idiomatic: His second son Huan was captured at Jianning, and his fate is unknown;

sentences.zh: 少子格，字壽平，見藝術傳。

translations.literal: his youngest son Ge, styled Shouping, appears in the Biographies of Artists.
translations.idiomatic: his youngest son Ge, styled Shouping, is treated in the Biographies of Artists.

sentences.zh: 郭金台，字幼隗，湘潭人，本姓陳氏，名湜。

translations.literal: Guo Jintai, styled Youwei, was a native of Xiangtan; his original surname was Chen and his name Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jintai, styled Youwei, was from Xiangtan. His original surname was Chen and his given name Shi.

sentences.zh: 年十五，遭家難，賴中表郭氏卵翼得脫，遂為繼。

translations.literal: At fifteen he suffered a family calamity; relying on the sheltering wings of his maternal cousin's Guo clan he escaped, and was then adopted into that line.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he suffered a family calamity. Sheltered by his maternal cousin's Guo clan he escaped, and was then adopted into that family.

sentences.zh: 弱冠有聲黌序間，萬曆間，兩中副車。

translations.literal: In early manhood he had a reputation among the schools; during Wanli he twice placed on the second list of the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In early manhood he won renown among the schools. During the Wanli reign he twice placed on the second list of the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 崇禎朝，屢以名薦，不起；

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign he was repeatedly recommended by reputation and did not rise;
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he was repeatedly recommended by name and declined office;

sentences.zh: 例授官，亦不拜。

translations.literal: when an office was granted by routine appointment, he also did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: when an office was granted by routine appointment, he likewise refused it.

sentences.zh: 既南渡，隆武鄉試登賢書，督師何騰蛟論薦，授職方郎中。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing, in the Longwu provincial examination he passed and entered the ranks of the worthy; Grand Coordinator He Tengjiao recommended him on merit and he was appointed director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward crossing he passed the Longwu provincial examination. Grand Coordinator He Tengjiao recommended him, and he was appointed director in the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 再起監軍僉事，有司敦迫，皆以母老病辭不就。

translations.literal: When again promoted to vice commissioner of military inspection, the local authorities pressed him urgently, but each time he declined on the grounds of his mother's age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: When he was again promoted to vice commissioner of military inspection, the local authorities pressed him urgently, but each time he declined on the grounds of his mother's age and illness.

sentences.zh: 避跡山中，然於時事多所論列。

translations.literal: He hid his tracks in the mountains, yet on current affairs he offered many pointed analyses.
translations.idiomatic: He hid himself in the mountains, yet continued to offer pointed analyses of current affairs.

sentences.zh: 一二枕戈泣血之士，崎嶇嶺海，經營措置，不遺餘力。

translations.literal: One or two men who slept with weapons at their pillows and wept blood, over rugged mountains and seas, managing affairs and making arrangements, spared no effort.
translations.idiomatic: He was among the handful who slept with weapons at their pillows and wept blood for the cause, traversing rugged mountains and seas and managing affairs with every ounce of strength.

sentences.zh: 當是時，潰卒猖獗，積尸盈野，百里無人煙。

translations.literal: At that time routed soldiers ran rampant; corpses piled in the fields; for a hundred li there was no sign of human habitation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time routed soldiers ran rampant, corpses piled the fields, and for a hundred li not a trace of human life remained.

sentences.zh: 金台請於督師，命偏裨主團練，力率鄉勇，鍛矛戟，峙芻糗，鄉人全活者以數万計。

translations.literal: Jintai petitioned the grand coordinator, had a subordinate officer take charge of militia training, vigorously led village braves, forged spears and halberds, stored fodder and dry provisions; villagers wholly saved numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jintai petitioned the grand coordinator and had a subordinate officer take charge of militia training. He vigorously led village braves, forged spears and halberds, and stockpiled fodder and dry provisions. Tens of thousands of villagers owed their survival to him.

sentences.zh: 清初，當局特疏薦於朝，力請得免。

translations.literal: In early Qing the authorities specially memorialized recommending him to court; he strongly petitioned and was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Qing the authorities specially memorialized recommending him to the throne, but he petitioned forcefully and won exemption from office.

sentences.zh: 晚授徒衡山，深衣幅巾，足不履戶外，絕口不談世事。

translations.literal: In later years he taught students at Hengshan, wore deep robes and a square cap, his feet never crossed the threshold, and he never spoke of worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he taught students at Hengshan, dressed in deep robes and a scholar's cap, never set foot outside his door, and never spoke of worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 惟論列當時殉難諸人，輒欷歔流涕。

translations.literal: Only when enumerating those who died for the cause at the time would he sigh and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Only when he spoke of those who had died for the cause would he sigh and weep.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年，以疾卒於家，年六十有七。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi he died of illness at home, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi he died of illness at home, at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 自題其墓曰「遺民郭某之墓」。

translations.literal: He inscribed his own tomb: "Tomb of the leftover subject, Master Guo."
translations.idiomatic: He inscribed his own tomb with the words "Tomb of the leftover subject, Master Guo."

sentences.zh: 著有石村詩文集，五經駢語，博物彙編。

translations.literal: He authored the Shicun Poetry and Prose Collection, Parallel Sayings on the Five Classics, and Compendium of Natural History.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Shicun Poetry and Prose Collection, Parallel Sayings on the Five Classics, and Compendium of Natural History.

sentences.zh: 硃之瑜，字魯興，號舜水，餘姚人，寄籍松江。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhiyu, styled Luxing, sobriquet Shunshui, was a native of Yuyao with registered domicile in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhiyu, styled Luxing and known as Shunshui, was from Yuyao and registered his domicile in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 少有志概，九歲喪父，哀毀逾禮。

translations.literal: From youth he had lofty ambition; at nine he lost his father, and his grief exceeded ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had lofty ambition. He lost his father at nine, and his grief exceeded what ritual prescribed.

sentences.zh: 及長，精研六經，特通毛詩。

translations.literal: When grown he deeply studied the Six Classics and was especially versed in the Mao version of the Book of Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he mastered the Six Classics and was especially versed in the Mao recension of the Book of Poetry.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末，以諸生兩奉徵闢，不就。

translations.literal: At the end of Chongzhen, as a licentiate he twice received imperial summons and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Chongzhen reign, though twice summoned to office as a licentiate, he declined both times.

sentences.zh: 福王建號江南，召授江西按察司副使，兼兵部職方司郎中，監方國安軍，之瑜力辭。

translations.literal: Prince Fu established his regime in Jiangnan and summoned him to be vice censor of the Jiangxi surveillance commission, concurrently director in the Bureau of Military Appointments, supervising Fang Guo'an's army; Zhiyu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Fu established his regime in Jiangnan, he summoned Zhiyu as vice censor of the Jiangxi surveillance commission and concurrent director in the Bureau of Military Appointments to supervise Fang Guo'an's army. Zhiyu firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 台省劾偃蹇不奉詔，將逮捕，乃走避舟山，與經略王翊相締結，密謀恢復。

translations.literal: The censorate impeached him for sluggishness in not obeying the edict and was about to arrest him; he fled to Zhoushan, allied with Grand Coordinator Wang Yi, and secretly plotted restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate impeached him for defying the summons and moved to arrest him. He fled to Zhoushan, allied with Grand Coordinator Wang Yi, and secretly plotted restoration.

sentences.zh: 渡海至日本，思乞師。

translations.literal: He crossed the sea to Japan, intending to beg for troops.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the sea to Japan, hoping to beg military aid.

sentences.zh: 魯王監國，累徵闢，皆不就。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu served as regent, he was repeatedly summoned and each time refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu served as regent, Zhiyu was repeatedly summoned to office and each time refused.

sentences.zh: 又赴安南，見國王，強令拜，不為屈，轉敬禮之。

translations.literal: He also went to Annam and met the king, who forced him to bow; he would not yield, and the king came instead to respect and honor him.
translations.idiomatic: He also went to Annam and met the king, who tried to force him to bow. He would not yield, and the king came instead to respect and honor him.

sentences.zh: 復至日本，時舟山既失，之瑜師友擁兵者，如硃永祐、吳鍾巒等皆已死節，乃決蹈海全節之志，遂留寓長崎。

translations.literal: He returned to Japan; Zhoushan had already fallen; Zhiyu's teachers and friends who held armies, such as Zhu Yongyou and Wu Zhongluan, had all died martyrs; he then resolved on drowning himself to preserve his integrity and stayed at Nagasaki.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Japan. Zhoushan had already fallen, and Zhiyu's teachers and friends who commanded troops—Zhu Yongyou, Wu Zhongluan, and others—had all died martyrs. He resolved to drown himself rather than compromise his integrity, then took up residence at Nagasaki.

sentences.zh: 日人安東守約等師事之，束脩敬養，始終不衰。

translations.literal: Japanese such as Ando Shuyaku took him as master, presenting tuition and supporting him with reverence, never diminishing to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese scholars such as Ando Shuyaku studied under him, presenting tuition and supporting him with reverence that never waned.

sentences.zh: 日本水戶侯源光國厚禮延聘，待以賓師，之瑜慨然赴焉。

translations.literal: Tokugawa Mitsukuni, lord of Mito, treated him with great courtesy and invited him, receiving him as guest and teacher; Zhiyu went forth resolutely.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Mitsukuni of Mito treated him with great courtesy and invited him, receiving him as both guest and teacher. Zhiyu went forth resolutely.

sentences.zh: 每引見談論，依經守義，曲盡忠告善道之意。

translations.literal: Whenever received in audience for discussion, he followed the classics and upheld righteousness, thoroughly fulfilling the intent of sincere counsel and the good way.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was received in audience for discussion, he followed the classics and upheld righteousness, offering counsel as sincere and thorough as a loyal minister's.

sentences.zh: 教授學者，循循不倦。

translations.literal: In teaching scholars he was patient and untiring.
translations.idiomatic: In teaching scholars he was patient and never weary.

sentences.zh: 日人重之瑜，禮養備至，特於壽日設養老之禮，奉几杖以祝。

translations.literal: The Japanese greatly valued Zhiyu and provided for him with complete courtesy; especially on his birthday they performed the rite of honoring the aged, presenting armrest and staff in blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese greatly valued Zhiyu and provided for him with every courtesy. On his birthday they performed the rite of honoring the aged, presenting an armrest and staff in blessing.

sentences.zh: 又為製明室衣冠使服之，並欲為起居第，之瑜再辭曰：「吾藉上公眷顧，孤踪海外，得養志守節，而保明室衣冠，感莫大焉！

translations.literal: They also made Ming court dress for him to wear and wished to build him a residence; Zhiyu declined twice, saying: "I rely on my lord's favor; alone and adrift overseas, I am able to nourish my will and keep my integrity, and to preserve Ming court dress—my gratitude is boundless!
translations.idiomatic: They also had Ming court dress made for him to wear and wished to build him a residence. Zhiyu declined twice, saying, "I rely on my lord's favor. Alone and adrift overseas, I am able to nourish my will, keep my integrity, and preserve Ming court dress—my gratitude is boundless!

sentences.zh: 吾祖宗墳墓，久為發掘，每念及此，五內慘烈。

translations.literal: My ancestors' graves have long been exhumed; whenever I think of this my innermost being is torn with anguish.
translations.idiomatic: My ancestors' graves have long been desecrated. Whenever I think of this, my heart is torn with anguish.

sentences.zh: 若豐屋而安居，豈我志乎？」

translations.literal: If I lived in a grand house and dwelt at ease in peace, would that be my intent?"
translations.idiomatic: If I lived in a grand house and dwelt at ease, would that accord with my intent?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: So they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: So they desisted.

sentences.zh: 之瑜為日人作學宮圖說，商榷古今，剖微索隱，使梓人依其圖而以木模焉，棟樑枅椽，莫不悉備。

translations.literal: Zhiyu made an illustrated explanation of the academy for the Japanese, discussing ancient and modern matters and analyzing the subtle and searching out the hidden; he had carpenters follow his diagram and make wooden models, beams, rafters, bracket-sets, and purlins all completely provided.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu drew up an illustrated explanation of the academy for the Japanese, discussing ancient and modern practice and analyzing every subtle detail. He had carpenters follow his diagrams and build wooden models with beams, rafters, bracket-sets, and purlins all complete.

sentences.zh: 而殿堂結構之法，梓人所不能通曉者，親指授之。

translations.literal: As for methods of hall construction that the carpenters could not fully understand, he personally instructed them.
translations.idiomatic: Where the carpenters could not grasp the methods of hall construction, he instructed them personally.

sentences.zh: 度量分寸，湊離機巧，教喻縝密，經歲而畢。

translations.literal: Measuring inches and fractions, fitting joints with ingenious craft, he taught with meticulous care and completed the work in a year.
translations.idiomatic: He measured every inch and fraction, fitted joints with ingenious precision, and taught with meticulous care until the work was finished within a year.

sentences.zh: 文廟、啟聖宮。

translations.literal: The Confucian temple and the Hall of the Sage's Birth.
translations.idiomatic: There were the Confucian temple and the Hall of the Sage's Birth.

sentences.zh: 明倫堂、尊經閣、學舍、進賢樓，廊廡射圃，門戶牆垣，皆極精巧。

translations.literal: The Hall of Bright Ethics, the Venerating Classics Pavilion, student dormitories, the Advancing Worthies Tower, corridors, the archery ground, gates, and walls—all were extremely refined.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Bright Ethics, the Venerating Classics Pavilion, student dormitories, the Advancing Worthies Tower, corridors, the archery ground, gates, and walls were all executed with exquisite refinement.

sentences.zh: 又造古祭器，先作古升、古尺，揣其稱勝，作簠、簋、籩、豆、登、鉶之屬。

translations.literal: He also made ancient ritual vessels; first he made the ancient sheng measure and ancient chi ruler, estimated their proportional weight, and made fu, gui, bian, dou, deng, xing, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He also recreated ancient ritual vessels. First he made the ancient sheng measure and chi ruler, estimated their proper proportions, and then fashioned fu, gui, bian, dou, deng, xing, and the like.

sentences.zh: 如周廟欹器，唐、宋以來，圖雖存而製莫傳，乃依圖考古，研覈其法，巧思默契，指畫精到。

translations.literal: Such as the tilted vessel of the Zhou temple: since Tang and Song, though diagrams survived the manufacture was not transmitted; he studied archaeology from the diagrams, examined the methods, harmonized ingenious thought, and gave instructions with precision.
translations.idiomatic: Take the tilted vessel of the Zhou temple: since Tang and Song times diagrams had survived but the craft had been lost. He studied the archaeology from the diagrams, examined the methods, and with ingenious insight gave instructions of exacting precision.

sentences.zh: 授之工師，或未洞達。

translations.literal: When passed to master craftsmen, sometimes they did not fully grasp it.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed the work to master craftsmen, sometimes they still did not fully grasp it.

sentences.zh: 復為揣輕重，定尺寸，關機運動，教之經年，不厭煩數，卒成之。

translations.literal: Again he estimated weight, fixed dimensions, and joint mechanism movement, taught for a year without wearying of repetition, and finally completed it.
translations.idiomatic: Again he estimated weight, fixed dimensions, and the moving joints of the mechanism, teaching for a full year without wearying of repetition until at last it was completed.

sentences.zh: 於是率儒學生，習釋奠禮，改定儀注，詳明禮節，學者皆通其梗概。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led Confucian students to practice the sacrificial rite, revised ritual procedures, clarified ritual etiquette, and scholars all understood the outline.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he led Confucian students in practicing the sacrificial rite, revised the ritual procedures, and clarified the etiquette until every scholar understood the essentials.

sentences.zh: 日人文教，為之彬彬焉。

translations.literal: Japanese culture and education thereby became refined.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese culture and education became refined thereby.

sentences.zh: 之瑜居日本二十餘年，年八十三卒，葬於日本長崎瑞龍山麓。

translations.literal: Zhiyu lived in Japan more than twenty years; he died at eighty-three and was buried at the foot of Ruilong Mountain in Nagasaki, Japan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu lived in Japan for more than twenty years. He died at eighty-three and was buried at the foot of Ruilong Mountain in Nagasaki.

sentences.zh: 日人諡曰文恭先生，立祠祀之，並護其墓，至今不衰。

translations.literal: The Japanese posthumously titled him Master Wengong, built a temple to worship him, and also protected his tomb—to this day without decline.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese posthumously honored him as Master Wengong, built a temple to worship him, and protected his tomb—a reverence that has not waned to this day.

sentences.zh: 之瑜嚴毅剛直，動必以禮。

translations.literal: Zhiyu was stern, resolute, and upright; every movement followed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyu was stern, resolute, and upright; every action accorded with ritual.

sentences.zh: 平居不苟言笑，唯言及國難，常切齒流涕。

translations.literal: In daily life he was not casual in speech or smile; only when speaking of the national calamity did he constantly gnash his teeth and weep.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he was never casual in speech or laughter. Only when the national calamity was mentioned would he gnash his teeth and weep.

sentences.zh: 魯王敕書，奉持隨身，未嘗示人，歿後始出，人皆服其深密謹厚雲。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu's edict letter he always carried on his person and never showed others; only after his death was it revealed, and people all admired his deep secrecy and careful integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He always carried the Prince of Lu's edict on his person and never showed it to anyone. Only after his death was it revealed, and all admired his secrecy and steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 著有文集二十五卷，釋奠儀註一卷，陽九述略一卷，安南供役紀事一卷。

translations.literal: He authored Collected Works in twenty-five juan, Sacrificial Ritual Procedures in one juan, Outline of the Yangjiu in one juan, and Record of Service in Annam in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Collected Works in twenty-five juan, Sacrificial Ritual Procedures in one juan, Outline of the Yangjiu in one juan, and Record of Service in Annam in one juan.

sentences.zh: 沈光文，字文開，一字斯菴，鄞人。

translations.literal: Shen Guangwen, styled Wenkai, also styled Si'an, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Guangwen, styled Wenkai and also known as Si'an, was from Yin.

sentences.zh: 少以明經貢太學，福王授太常博士，浮海至長垣，晉工部郎。

translations.literal: In youth he passed the classics examination and entered the Imperial Academy; Prince Fu appointed him Erudite of the Grand Master of Ceremonies; he crossed the sea to Changyuan and was promoted to director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he passed the classics examination and entered the Imperial Academy. Prince Fu appointed him Erudite of the Grand Master of Ceremonies. He crossed the sea to Changyuan and was promoted to director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 閩師潰而北，扈從不及。

translations.literal: The Fujian armies were routed and fled north; he could not follow in escort.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian armies were routed and fled north, and he could not join the royal escort.

sentences.zh: 聞粵中建號，乃走肇慶，累遷太僕卿。

translations.literal: Hearing that Guangdong had established a regime, he went to Zhaoqing and was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Guangdong had established a regime, he went to Zhaoqing and was repeatedly promoted until he became Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 由潮陽航海至金門，閩督李率泰方招徠故國遺臣，密遣使以書幣招之，光文焚書返幣。

translations.literal: From Chaoyang he sailed to Kinmen; Fujian governor Li Shuatai was then recruiting former ministers of the old dynasty and secretly sent an envoy with letter and gifts to invite him; Guangwen burned the letter and returned the gifts.
translations.idiomatic: From Chaoyang he sailed to Kinmen. The Fujian governor Li Shuatai was then recruiting former ministers of the fallen dynasty and secretly sent an envoy with a letter and gifts to win him over. Guangwen burned the letter and returned the gifts.

sentences.zh: 知粵事不可支，卜居於泉州海口，浮家泛宅。

translations.literal: Knowing that affairs in Guangdong could not hold, he chose to live at the harbor mouth of Quanzhou, floating home upon the waters.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Guangdong cause could not hold, he chose to live at the harbor mouth of Quanzhou, making his home upon the water.

sentences.zh: 忽颶風大作，舟人失維，飄泊至台灣。

translations.literal: Suddenly a great typhoon arose; the boatmen lost their moorings and drifted to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a great typhoon arose. The boatmen lost their moorings and were driven to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 時鄭成功尚未至，而台灣為荷蘭所據，光文受一廛以居，與中土音耗隔絕。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Chenggong had not yet arrived, and Taiwan was held by the Dutch; Guangwen received one homestead to dwell in and was cut off from news of the central lands.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong had not yet arrived, and Taiwan was held by the Dutch. Guangwen received a homestead to live on and was cut off from all news of the mainland.

sentences.zh: 成功克台灣，知光文在，大喜，以賓禮見。

translations.literal: Chenggong captured Taiwan, learned Guangwen was there, was greatly pleased, and received him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenggong captured Taiwan and learned that Guangwen was there, he was overjoyed and received him with the ceremony due a guest.

sentences.zh: 時海上諸遺老，多依成功入台，光文與握手相勞苦。

translations.literal: At that time many elderly loyalists at sea relied on Chenggong to enter Taiwan; Guangwen shook hands with them, exchanging accounts of hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Many elderly loyalists at sea had followed Chenggong to Taiwan. Guangwen shook hands with them and exchanged accounts of their hardships.

sentences.zh: 成功致廩餼，且以田宅贍之。

translations.literal: Chenggong provided stipends and also granted fields and a residence to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong provided him with stipends and granted fields and a residence for his support.

sentences.zh: 成功卒，子錦嗣，改父之臣與政，軍亦日削。

translations.literal: Chenggong died; his son Jing succeeded, changed his father's ministers and policies, and the armies also daily weakened.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenggong died, his son Zheng Jing succeeded him, replaced his father's ministers and policies, and the armies dwindled day by day.

sentences.zh: 光文作賦諷之，幾不測。

translations.literal: Guangwen wrote a fu satirizing him and nearly suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwen wrote a fu satirizing him and nearly came to grief for it.

sentences.zh: 乃變服為浮屠，逃入台北鄙，結茅羅漢門山中以居，山旁有伽溜灣者，番社也。

translations.literal: He then changed dress to become a monk, fled into the remote north of Taipei, built a thatched hut in the Luohan Gate mountains to dwell, and beside the mountain was Galao Bay, an aboriginal settlement.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his dress and became a monk, fled into the remote north of Taipei, and built a thatched hut in the Luohan Gate mountains to live in. Beside the mountain lay Galao Bay, an aboriginal settlement.

sentences.zh: 光文教授生徒自給，不足，則濟以醫。

translations.literal: Guangwen taught students to support himself; when insufficient he supplemented with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwen supported himself by teaching students; when that was not enough, he supplemented his income with medicine.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「吾二十載飄零絕島，棄墳墓不顧者，不過欲完發以見先皇帝於地下耳，而卒不克，命也夫！」

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "My twenty years adrift on an isolated isle, abandoning my graves without regard—all because I wished only to keep my hair intact and meet the former emperor underground, yet ultimately could not—fate indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "Twenty years adrift on this isolated isle, abandoning my ancestors' graves—all because I wished only to keep my hair and meet the former emperor in the world below. Yet in the end I could not. Fate indeed!"

sentences.zh: 已而錦卒，諸鄭復禮之如故。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jing died, and the various Zheng again treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zheng Jing died, and the Zheng clan again treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 康熙癸丑年，王師下台灣，閩督姚啟聖招之，光文辭。

translations.literal: In the guichou year of Kangxi the imperial army descended on Taiwan; Fujian governor Yao Qisheng recruited him, and Guangwen declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year of Kangxi the imperial army took Taiwan. The Fujian governor Yao Qisheng invited him, and Guangwen declined.

sentences.zh: 啟聖貽書問訊曰：「管寧無恙？」

translations.literal: Qisheng sent a letter greeting him, saying: "Is Guan Ning well?"
translations.idiomatic: Qisheng sent a letter of greeting that read, "Is Guan Ning well?"

sentences.zh: 且許遣人送歸鄞，會啟聖卒，不果。

translations.literal: and also promised to send someone to escort him home to Yin; but Qisheng died and it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: He also promised to send someone to escort him home to Yin, but Qisheng died before it could be done.

sentences.zh: 而諸羅令李麟光，賢者也，為粟肉之繼，旬日一候門下。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Zhuluo, Li Linguang, was a worthy man; he provided grain and meat in succession and every ten days visited his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linguang, magistrate of Zhuluo, was a worthy man. He sent grain and meat in steady supply and visited Guangwen's gate every ten days.

sentences.zh: 時耆宿已盡，而寓公漸集，乃與宛陵韓文琦，關中趙行可，無錫華袞、鄭廷桂，榕城林奕丹，山陽宗城，螺陽王際慧等結詩社，所稱福台新詠者也。

translations.literal: At that time the elder generation was already gone, while expatriates gradually gathered; he then with Han Wenqi of Wannings, Zhao Xingke of Guanzhong, Hua Gun and Zheng Tinggui of Wuxi, Lin Yidan of Rongcheng, Zong Cheng of Shanyang, Wang Jihui of Luoyang, and others formed a poetry society called New Poems of Fortunate Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: The elder generation was already gone, but expatriates were gradually gathering. He formed a poetry society with Han Wenqi of Wannings, Zhao Xingke of Guanzhong, Hua Gun and Zheng Tinggui of Wuxi, Lin Yidan of Rongcheng, Zong Cheng of Shanyang, Wang Jihui of Luoyang, and others—the group known as New Poems of Fortunate Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於諸羅。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died at Zhuluo.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at Zhuluo.

sentences.zh: 陳士京，字佛莊，先世本奉化硃氏，遷鄞，改姓陳。

translations.literal: Chen Shijing, styled Fozhuang; his ancestors were originally of the Zhu clan of Fenghua, migrated to Yin, and changed their surname to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shijing, styled Fozhuang, was descended from the Zhu clan of Fenghua. His ancestors migrated to Yin and changed their surname to Chen.

sentences.zh: 熊汝霖薦授職方司郎中，監三衢總兵陳謙軍。

translations.literal: Xiong Rulin recommended him and he was appointed director in the Bureau of Military Appointments, supervising the army of Chen Qian, commander of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Rulin recommended him, and he was appointed director in the Bureau of Military Appointments to supervise the army of Chen Qian, commander of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 謙使閩，偕行，而唐、魯方爭頒詔事，謙死，遂遯之海上。

translations.literal: Qian was sent on mission to Fujian and Shijing went with him; the Tang and Lu courts were then competing to issue edicts; Qian died, and Shijing then fled to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was sent on mission to Fujian and Shijing went with him. The Tang and Lu courts were then competing to issue edicts. When Qian died, Shijing fled to the sea.

sentences.zh: 鄭芝龍聞名，令與其子成功遊，芝龍以閩降，成功不肯從，異軍特起，士京實讚之。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhilong heard his fame and had him associate with his son Chenggong; Zhilong surrendered Fujian, Chenggong refused to follow, rose independently with a separate army, and Shijing in fact praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhilong, hearing of his reputation, had him associate with his son Chenggong. When Zhilong surrendered Fujian, Chenggong refused to follow and raised an independent force. Shijing openly praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 已而汝霖奉魯王室，復以公義說成功，始致寓公之敬。

translations.literal: Later Rulin served the Prince of Lu's court and again used public duty to persuade Chenggong; only then did he earn the respect due a guest minister.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Rulin served the Prince of Lu's court, he again appealed to Chenggong on grounds of public duty, and only then did Shijing earn the respect due a guest minister.

sentences.zh: 會魯王上表粵中，成功亦欲啟事於粵，使士京往，加都御史，歸。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu submitted a memorial to Guangdong, Chenggong also wished to open affairs in Guangdong and sent Shijing; he was promoted to censor-in-chief and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu submitted a memorial to Guangdong, Chenggong also wished to open relations there and sent Shijing. Shijing was promoted to censor-in-chief and then returned.

sentences.zh: 魯王入浙，特留閩，與成功相結，以為後圖。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu entered Zhejiang; Shijing was specially left in Fujian to ally with Chenggong for future plans.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu entered Zhejiang, Shijing was specially left in Fujian to ally with Chenggong for future plans.

sentences.zh: 成功盛以恢復自任，賓禮遺臣，其最致敬者，尚書盧若騰，侍郎王忠孝，都御史章朝薦，及徐孚遠、沈光文，與士京數人而已。

translations.literal: Chenggong greatly took restoration as his charge and treated loyalist ministers with guest ceremony; those he most honored were Ministers Lu Ruoteng and Wang Zhongxiao, Censor Zhang Chaojian, and Xu Fuyuan, Shen Guangwen, and Shijing—only a few.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong took the restoration of the dynasty as his great mission and received loyalist ministers with guest ceremony. Those he most honored were the ministers Lu Ruoteng and Wang Zhongxiao, the censor Zhang Chaojian, Xu Fuyuan, Shen Guangwen, and Shijing—only a handful in all.

sentences.zh: 久之，見海師無功，粵事亦日壞，乃築鹿石山房於鼓浪嶼中，感物賦詩以自遣。

translations.literal: After a long time, seeing the naval forces achieve nothing and Guangdong affairs also daily worsen, he built the Lushi Mountain Hermitage on Gulangyu and, moved by things around him, wrote poetry to console himself.
translations.idiomatic: After long years, seeing the naval forces achieve nothing and the Guangdong cause daily worsen, he built the Lushi Mountain Hermitage on Gulangyu and wrote poetry inspired by the world around him to console himself.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 吳祖錫，字佩遠，吳江人。

translations.literal: Wu Zuxi, styled Peiyuan, was a native of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zuxi, styled Peiyuan, was from Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎壬午副貢。

translations.literal: In the renchen year of Chongzhen he placed on the second list of the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the renchen year of Chongzhen he placed on the second list of the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 時中原大亂，料京師必危，預謀勤王。

translations.literal: At that time the central plains were in great chaos; he judged the capital would surely be endangered and premeditated rushing to aid the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The central plains were in chaos. He judged that the capital would surely fall and began planning to rush to the throne's aid.

sentences.zh: 欲身任浙西，以浙東屬之許都，約未定而變作，故鎮臣陳洪範隨王師下江南，與有舊，自言其降出於不得已，而以奇策告祖錫，立出遺產四萬金畀之。

translations.literal: He wished personally to take charge of western Zhejiang and assign eastern Zhejiang to Xu Du; the agreement was not settled when crisis erupted; thus garrison commander Chen Hongfan followed the Qing army south to Jiangnan, had old ties with him, said himself that his surrender was unavoidable, and told a secret strategy to Zuxi, immediately giving his inheritance of forty thousand gold to him.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to take charge of western Zhejiang himself and assign eastern Zhejiang to Xu Du, but before the agreement was settled crisis erupted. The garrison commander Chen Hongfan followed the Qing south into Jiangnan. They had old ties, and Hongfan said his surrender had been unavoidable. He confided a secret strategy to Zuxi and immediately handed over his inheritance of forty thousand taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 已而薙發令下，遽委之去，改名鉏，字稽田。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the hair-shaving order was issued; he abruptly left it behind, changed his name to Chu, styled Jitian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the hair-shaving order was issued. He abruptly abandoned the plan, changed his name to Chu, and styled himself Jitian.

sentences.zh: 從陳子龍、徐孚遠謀恢復。

translations.literal: With Chen Zilong and Xu Fuyuan he plotted restoration.
translations.idiomatic: With Chen Zilong and Xu Fuyuan he plotted restoration.

sentences.zh: 偵事杭州，為仇家縛送江寧，羈繫獄中，复髡而縱之。

translations.literal: Spying on affairs at Hangzhou, he was bound by an enemy family and sent to Jiangning, imprisoned, re-shaved, and released.
translations.idiomatic: While spying on affairs at Hangzhou, he was seized by an enemy family and sent to Jiangning. He was imprisoned, shaved again, and then released.

sentences.zh: 魯王授職方郎中，桂王亦官之如魯，仍往來吳、越間。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu appointed him director in the Bureau of Military Appointments; the Prince of Gui also gave him the same rank, and he still traveled between Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu appointed him director in the Bureau of Military Appointments, and the Prince of Gui gave him the same rank. He continued to travel between Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 副將馮源淮駐軍嘉興，乃與結納，冀有所為。

translations.literal: Vice general Feng Yuanhuai stationed his army at Jiaxing; Zuxi allied with him, hoping to accomplish something.
translations.idiomatic: The vice general Feng Yuanhuai had stationed his army at Jiaxing. Zuxi allied with him, hoping to accomplish something.

sentences.zh: 其部屬董某司诇察，馮耳目也，亦故與厚善。

translations.literal: His subordinate Dong served as scout and intelligence officer—Feng's eyes and ears—and was also formerly on close terms with Zuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's subordinate Dong served as scout and intelligence officer—Feng's eyes and ears—and had also been on close terms with Zuxi.

sentences.zh: 比孚遠歸自海外，有所謀，密館之。

translations.literal: When Fuyuan returned from overseas with some plan, Zuxi secretly lodged him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Fuyuan returned from overseas with a plan in hand, Zuxi secretly housed him.

sentences.zh: 事稍聞於馮，馮遣董詣問，祖錫遽前握其手曰：「徐公在此，若欲見之乎？」

translations.literal: The matter was slightly heard by Feng; Feng sent Dong to inquire; Zuxi immediately stepped forward, grasped his hand, and said: "Master Xu is here—do you wish to see him?"
translations.idiomatic: Word of the matter reached Feng, who sent Dong to inquire. Zuxi immediately stepped forward, grasped his hand, and said, "Master Xu is here. Do you wish to see him?"

sentences.zh: 董驚曰：「徐公果在此，顧肯令我見耶？」

translations.literal: Dong startled, said: "If Master Xu is truly here, would he really let me see him?"
translations.idiomatic: Dong was astonished. "If Master Xu is truly here, would he really let me see him?"

sentences.zh: 即引見，董叩頭泣下，道其鄉慕，矢不相負。

translations.literal: He immediately introduced them; Dong kowtowed and wept, expressed his hometown admiration, and vowed not to betray.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxi immediately introduced them. Dong kowtowed and wept, spoke of his admiration from their home region, and vowed never to betray them.

sentences.zh: 因以譌言報馮，而陰遣弋船衛孚遠浮海去。

translations.literal: He then reported false words to Feng, while secretly sending an escort boat to guard Fuyuan's departure overseas.
translations.idiomatic: He then fed Feng false reports while secretly dispatching an escort boat to see Xu Fuyuan safely overseas.

sentences.zh: 海師入江，祖錫實導之，且連歲在金陵，隱為之助。

translations.literal: When the naval forces entered the Yangtze, Zuxi actually guided them, and for successive years at Jinling secretly assisted them.
translations.idiomatic: When the naval forces entered the Yangtze, Zuxi guided them in person, and for years at Jinling he secretly assisted them.

sentences.zh: 乃復遭刊章，事解，志不稍挫。

translations.literal: He again suffered a published warrant; the affair was resolved, and his resolve was not slightly broken.
translations.idiomatic: He again faced a published warrant for his arrest, but when the affair was resolved his resolve did not waver in the least.

sentences.zh: 將詣滇南，而先之鄖陽。

translations.literal: About to go to southern Yunnan, he first went to Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to go to southern Yunnan and first went to Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 時鄖陽十三營，尚保殘寨，乃勸出師撓楚以救滇。

translations.literal: At that time the thirteen camps at Yunyang still held remnant fortresses; he advised sending troops to harass Chu to rescue Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteen camps at Yunyang still held remnant fortresses. He urged them to march out and harass Chu to relieve Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 顧十三營已疲敝，不能用其策也。

translations.literal: But the thirteen camps were already exhausted and could not use his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: But the thirteen camps were already exhausted and could not adopt his strategy.

sentences.zh: 桂王既入緬甸，思追從，道阻，不得達。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gui having already entered Burma, Zuxi wished to pursue and follow, but the road was blocked and he could not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Gui had fled into Burma, Zuxi wished to follow him, but the road was blocked and he could not reach him.

sentences.zh: 復返吳。

translations.literal: He returned again to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He returned once more to Wu.

sentences.zh: 遊中州，更由秦入楚，卒無所遇。

translations.literal: He traveled through the Central Plain, then from Qin entered Chu, and in the end met with nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled through the Central Plain, then from Qin into Chu, and in the end found no opening for his cause.

sentences.zh: 康熙己未，客膠州大竹山，鬱鬱靡所騁​​。

translations.literal: In the jiwei year of Kangxi he lodged as a guest at Dazhu Mountain in Jiaozhou, depressed with nowhere to pour forth his will.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year of Kangxi he lodged as a guest at Dazhu Mountain in Jiaozhou, depressed and with nowhere to turn his energies.

sentences.zh: 會懷宗忌日，慟哭嘔血死，遺命藁葬山中，年​​六十有二。

translations.literal: It happened to be the memorial day of the Huizong Emperor; he wailed in grief until he vomited blood and died, leaving instructions to be buried in straw matting in the mountains, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: On the memorial day of the Huizong Emperor he wailed until he vomited blood and died, leaving instructions for a simple burial in the mountains; he was sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 距明亡已三十有五年矣。

translations.literal: It was already thirty-five years since the fall of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-five years had passed since the fall of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 凡明末三王遺臣逸士，其初或起義，或言事，各有所謀，其後或蹈海，或居夷，志不少沮，皆先後雲亡。

translations.literal: In all, the surviving ministers and reclusive scholars of the three Ming princes at the dynasty's end—at first some raised righteous armies, some remonstrated in office, each with his own design; afterward some went to sea, some dwelt among foreigners, their wills never much diminished—all passed away one after another like clouds dispersing.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the loyalist ministers and reclusive scholars who served the three Ming princes at the dynasty's end—some at first raised armies, some remonstrated at court, each with his own design; later some took to the sea, some lived among foreigners, their resolve scarcely broken—all passed away in turn like clouds dispersing.

sentences.zh: 及祖錫死，徐枋為之傳曰：「自吳子歿，而天下絕援溺之望。」

translations.literal: When Zuxi died, Xu Fang wrote his biography, saying: "Since Master Wu's death, the world has lost hope of rescuing the drowning."
translations.idiomatic: When Zuxi died, Xu Fang wrote his biography, saying: "Since Master Wu's death, the world has lost all hope of rescuing the drowning."

sentences.zh: 亦可悲矣！

translations.literal: How lamentable as well!
translations.idiomatic: How lamentable!

sentences.zh: 故以附於明末遺臣之末。

translations.literal: Therefore he is appended at the end of the late-Ming surviving ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore his account is appended at the end of the late-Ming surviving ministers.
